translations.reference: There were also toilets in ancient Egypt, Persia and China. In Roman civilization, toilets were sometimes part of public bath houses where men and women were together in mixed company.
translations.hypothesis: They also had public bathhouses in ancient Egypt, Persia and China. Under Roman rule, public bathhouses were sometimes part of a public latrine where men and women would meet.

translations.source: Mgbe ikporo mmadu onye no otutu puku maili site n’ebe ino , ihe iji bu igwe satalaiti.
translations.reference: When you call someone who is thousands of miles away, you are using a satellite.
translations.hypothesis: When people communicate with one another over great distances, they use satellites.

translations.source: Satilaịti nọ n'ikuku na enweta oku ma zighachi ya n'ala na ntabi anya.
translations.reference: The satellite in space gets the call and then reflects it back down, almost instantly.
translations.hypothesis: Satellites in orbit receive radio signals and bounce them back down to Earth.

translations.source: E ji ụgbọelu rọkeetị zije satilaịti n'ikuku. Ndị ọka mmụta sayensị na eji igwe nyocha kpakpando afụ ụzọ n'ikuku mpụga ụwa n'ihi na igwe ụwa anyị na arọgharị ụfọdụ ọkụ anyị na ahụ.
translations.reference: The satellite was sent into space by a rocket. Scientists use telescopes in space because the Earth’s atmosphere distorts some of our light and view.
translations.hypothesis: Satellites are put into orbit using rockets. Scientists use telescopes to look at things in space because the light from those things has traveled a very long way to reach us.

translations.source: O na-ewe nnukwu rọketi gafere ụkwụ otu narị n’elu itinye otu satịlaịtị na teliskop n’eluụwa.
translations.reference: It takes a giant rocket over a 100 feet high to put a satellite or telescope in space.
translations.hypothesis: It launches a large rocket beyond the atmosphere to put a satellite or telescope into orbit.

translations.source: Wiilu agbanweela ụwa n'ụdị enweghị atụ. Ihe kachasị ukwu nke wiilu merela anyị bụ na o nyere anyị ụzọ njem dị mfe ma dị ọsịsọ karịa.
translations.reference: The wheel has changed the world in incredible ways. The biggest thing that the wheel has done for us is given us much easier and faster transportation.
translations.hypothesis: The wheel has changed the world in countless ways. The greatest impact of the wheel is that it allowed us to travel quickly and easily.

translations.source: O wetegoro anyị ụgbọoloko, ụgbọala na ọtụtụ akụrụngwa njem dị iche iche.
translations.reference: It has brought us the train, the car, and many other transportation devices.
translations.hypothesis: It gave us cars, trucks, and all kinds of other vehicles.

translations.source: N'okpuru ha bụ ụmụ nwamba ha ọkara na-eri anụoriri ha ọkara nke nwere ike isi na oke bekee ruo na ele nakwa mgbada.
translations.reference: Under them are more medium sized cats that eat medium sized prey ranging from rabbits to antelopes and deer.
translations.hypothesis: Below them are the half-fish, half-chicken-like creatures that can grow up to 10 feet long and weigh up to 20 pounds.

translations.source: N’ikpeazụ, e nwere ọtụtụ obere nwamba (gụnyere anụ ụlọ nwamba furu efu) na-eri ọtụtụ obere ụmụ anụmanụ dị ka ụmụ ahụhụ, oke, ngwere, na nnụnụ.
translations.reference: Finally, there are many small cats (including loose pet cats) that eat the far more numerous small prey like insects, rodents, lizards, and birds.
translations.hypothesis: Finally, there are many small carnivores (including jackals and foxes) that prey on small mammals such as hares, rodents, hedgehogs and birds.

translations.source: Ihe nzuzo nke ọganihu ha bụ gburugburu ebe obibi, ọrụ nwamba niile ji nke na egbochi ịsọmpi ha na ndị ọzọ.
translations.reference: The secret to their success is the concept of the niche, a special job each cat holds that keeps it from competing with others.
translations.hypothesis: The key to their success is their eco-friendly, all-natural product that stands out from the competition.

translations.source: Ọdụm bụ nwamba kachasị emekọrịta n'onwe ha, na-ebi na nnukwu òtù akpọrọ nganga.
translations.reference: Lions are the most social cats, living in large groups called prides.
translations.hypothesis: Ants are highly social insects, living in large colonies called ant farms.

translations.source: Mpako gasị bụ otu ruo atọ ụmụ nwoke tozuru oke metụtaranụ mejupụtara ya, yana ụmụ nwanyị na ụmụ ya dị ọtụtụ dị ka iri atọ.
translations.reference: Prides are made up of one to three related adult males, along with as many as thirty females and cubs.
translations.hypothesis: The attack involved a suicide bomber and three gunmen, while dozens of women and children were also abducted.

translations.source: Ndị nwanyị na-emetụtakarị nke ukwu n’onwe ha, n’ibu otu nnukwu ezinụlọ nke ụmụnne nwanyị na ụmụ nwa nwanyị.
translations.reference: The females are usually closely related to each other, being a large family of sisters and daughters.
translations.hypothesis: Women are often primary caregivers, for both children and the elderly.

translations.source: Ezinụlọ Ọdụm na-akpa agwa ka ezinụlọ oke nkịta ọhịa maọbụ nkịta ụlọ, anụ ndị nwere oyiyi dị ịtụ n'anya nye Ọdụm (mana odịghị otu a n'ebe nnukwu nwamba ndị ọzọ nọ) n'omume, ma bụrụ ihe oke iyi egwu nye ihe ọbụla ha na-achụ na nta.
translations.reference: Lion prides act much like packs of wolves or dogs, animals surprisingly similar to lions (but not other big cats) in behavior, and also very deadly to their prey.
translations.hypothesis: The dingo is a wild dog-like animal, with a distinctive reddish-brown coat (though some are black and white), and a shy nature, which makes it a poor guard animal, and a poor hunter for anything larger than a small rodent.

translations.source: Ome ihe egwuregwu zuruoke nkeoma, agu ahu ga enyili elu (obu ezie na obughi nkeoma), gwuo mmiri, maa-amaa garuo ebe di oke anya ma doo okpukpu ise dika ike mmadu di ike nwere ike ido.
translations.reference: A well rounded athlete, the tiger can climb (though not well), swim, leap great distances and pull with five times the force of a strong human.
translations.hypothesis: Some of the more advanced games, such as Quake, are very violent, involve a great deal of shooting, and are set in fantastic and violent worlds and pit the player against hordes of enemies as well as other human players.

translations.source: Agụ nọ n’otu otu (Genus Panthera) dika ọdụm, owuru, na jaguar. Nwamba anọ ndị a bụ naanị ndị nwere ike ime mbigbọ.
translations.reference: The tiger is in the same group (Genus Panthera) as lions, leopards, and jaguars. These four cats are the only ones who can roar.
translations.hypothesis: The genus Panthera includes the lion, tiger, leopard and jaguar. These four species are the only ones capable of producing a true roar.

translations.source: Ụja agụ adịghị ka mgbọpụta n'uju ụja ọdụm, mana ọ dị nnọọ ka okwu e kwuputara n'iti mkpu.
translations.reference: The tiger's roar is not like the full-voiced roar of a lion, but more like a sentence of snarly, shouted words.
translations.hypothesis: The clicks are not like any sounds in the tonal languages, but are more like sounds made in the middle of a shout.

translations.source: Ona amasi Ocelot iri obere umu-anumanu. Ha ga anwuchi enwe, agwo, oke na nnunu ma ha nwee ike. Oka-na-onuogugu anu anumanu nile Ocelot na achu-nta di obere nnukwu karia ka odi.
translations.reference: Ocelots like to eat small animals. They will catch monkeys, snakes, rodents and birds if they can. Almost all of the animals that the ocelot hunts are far smaller than it is.
translations.hypothesis: Ocelots are about the size of a small house cat. They are stocky and long-tailed, with large paws and short, rounded ears. The ocelot is the largest of the small-spotted cats.

translations.source: Ndị oke mmụta sayensị cheere na nwamba Oselọt ji isi esochi ma na-achọta anụ ha ga eri, site na ịkpọkwa imi n'ala iji site ebe ha gara.
translations.reference: Scientists think that ocelots follow and find animals to eat (prey) by smell, sniffing for where they've been on the ground.
translations.hypothesis: Scientists believe that the Ostrich's head is used to help it to see where it is going, as well as sniffing the ground to find out where the next meal is coming from.

translations.source: Ha na-ahụ ụzọ nke ọma n'abalị, ma na ejegharịkwa na nzuzo karịa. Oselọotụ na agwakọta onwe ha na gburugburu ha iji nwude anụ ha na achụ.
translations.reference: They can see very well in the dark with night vision, and move very stealthily, too. Ocelots hunt their prey by blending in with their surroundings then pouncing on their prey.
translations.hypothesis: They can see well at night and move almost silently.Leopards are solitary except when mating or when females are raising their young.

translations.source: Mgbe ọbụla ụmụ obere ihe dị ndụ (obere ọnụ ọgụgụ yiri onwe ha) si na ndị otu ha pụọ (dịka ha gafee ugwu, osimiri, maọbụ gaa n'agwaetiti ọzọ ebe ọ ga-ara ahụ isi laghachi) ha ga-achọta onwe ha na gburugburu di iche ọtụtụ mgbe.
translations.reference: When a small group of living things (a small population) gets separated from the main population that they came from (like if they move over a mountain range or a river, or if they move to a new island so that they can't easily move back) they will often find themselves in a different environment than they were in before.
translations.hypothesis: When small groups of animals (a few individuals) get separated from their group (e.g. by crossing a mountain range, a sea, or by getting lost) they may find themselves in a new environment.

translations.source: Gburugburu ọhụrụ a nwere akụrụngwa dị iche ma ndị ịsọmpi dị iche, n'ihi nke a ọnụọgụgụ ọhụrụ ahụ kwesịrị inwe akụrụngwa dị iche maọbụ ihe mmegharị ọzọ ga eme ya ka ọbụrụ onye ịsọmpi dị ike karịa ka ọdịbu.
translations.reference: This new environment has different resources and different competitors, so the new population will need different features or adaptations to be a strong competitor than what they had needed before.
translations.hypothesis: The new environment has different tools and different competitors, so the new startup has to have different tools or different moves to be a stronger competitor than the old one.

translations.source: Ọnụọgụgụ nke izizi agbanwebeghị maọlị, ha ka chọrọ ihe mmegharị dịka nke mgbe mbụ.
translations.reference: The original population hasn't changed at all, they still need the same adaptations as before.
translations.hypothesis: The original numbers were not changed and still required the same movement as the original.

translations.source: Ka oge na-aga, dịka gburugburu ha ọhụrụ bidoro mawa ha ahụ, oyiyi ha na ndị ha hapụrụ ebido na-ebelata.
translations.reference: Over time, as the new population begins to adapt to their new environment, they start to look less and less like the other population.
translations.hypothesis: As time went on, and as the new environment began to take hold, the pictures of the ones they left behind began to fade.

translations.source: Mgbe puku afọ maọbụ rịị nde afọ ụfọdụ gasịrị, otu abụọ a ga adị nnọọ iche ruo oke ebe agaghịzị akpọ ha abụọ otu ụdị.
translations.reference: Eventually, after thousands or even millions of years, the two populations will look so different that they can't be called the same species.
translations.hypothesis: After a few thousand or million years, the two will be so different that they will no longer be considered the same type.

translations.source: Anyi na-akpọ usoro a speciation, nke pụtara nguzobe nke ụdị okike ọhụụ. Speciation bụ nsonaazụ a na-apụghị ịgbagha agbagha na akụkụ dị oke mkpa nke evolushọn.
translations.reference: We call this process speciation, which just means the formation of new species. Speciation is an unavoidable consequence and a very important part of evolution.
translations.hypothesis: We call this process speciation, which means the formation of a new species. Speciation is an inevitable consequence of the major forces of evolution.

translations.source: Osisi na-eme ikuku oksigin nke mmadụ na-ekuru, ma ha na e kubanye carbon-dioxide nke mmadụ na-ekufu ume (ya bụ, na-ekufu ume).
translations.reference: Plants make oxygen which humans breathe, and they take in carbon-dioxide which humans exhale (that is, breathe out).
translations.hypothesis: Plants produce the oxygen that people breathe, and they consume carbon dioxide, a gas that people breathe out.

translations.source: Akụmakụ osisi na emepụta nri nke ha site n’anyanwụ site n’aka fotosintesis. Ha na-enyekwa ndo.
translations.reference: Plants make their food from the sun by photosynthesis. They also provide shade.
translations.hypothesis: Plants make their own food from sunlight through photosynthesis. They also provide oxygen.

translations.source: Anyị ji osisi eme ụlọ na akwa. Ọtụtụ nri anyị na-eri bụ osisi. Ewepụ osisi, anụmanụ agaghị adị ndụ.
translations.reference: We make our houses from plants and make clothes from plants. Most foods that we eat are plants. Without plants, animals could not survive.
translations.hypothesis: We build our homes and make our clothes from plants. Many of the foods we eat are plants. Without plants, animals would not be able to live.

translations.source: Mosasaurus bụbu isi n'anụ na-eri anụ n’oge ya, nke a mere na onweghi ihe na-atụ ya egwu, karịa mosasaurs ibe ya.
translations.reference: Mosasaurus was the apex predator of its time, so it feared nothing, except other mosasaurs.
translations.hypothesis: The Mosasaur was the top predator of its time, mostly due to its size, which made it a match for any other mosasaurs.

translations.source: Agba ogologo ya bụ nke emejupụtara n'iji ihe karịrị eze dị aguba-nkọ iri asaa, yana òtú òtù mmezi n'elu ọnụ ya, nke pụtara na ọ nweghị ụzọ mgbapụ maka ihe ọ bụla gafere n'ụzọ ya.
translations.reference: Its long jaws were studded with more than 70 razor-sharp teeth, along with an extra set in the roof of its mouth, meaning that there was no escape for anything that crossed its path.
translations.hypothesis: Its length is made up of more than seventy-seven individual blocks, with a slight inward slope, meaning that there are no steps up or down anywhere along its length.

translations.source: Onweghị anyị anya, mana ọ dịka onwere ire abụọ. Ọ na eri mbe mmiri, nnukwu azụ, anụ ndị yiri ya, onwekwara ike na eri ụdị nke ya.
translations.reference: We don't know for sure, but it may have had a forked tongue. Its diet included turtles, large fish, other mosasaurs, and it may even have been a cannibal.
translations.hypothesis: It is not known for certain, but it seems likely that it had two hearts. It ate plants, large fish, and possibly other animals, and was probably able to digest cellulose.

translations.source: Ọ wakpọkwara ihe ọ bụla banyere n’ime mmiri ahụ; ọbụná nnukwu dainosọọ dị ka T. rex abụghị atụ n’ebe ọ nọ.
translations.reference: It also attacked anything that entered the water; even a giant dinosaur such as T. rex would be no match for it.
translations.hypothesis: He also reported finding no evidence of any marine reptile; even large dinosaurs like T. rex are conspicuously absent.

translations.source: Ka anyị maara nke ọma imirikiti nri ha, ndị Rom nwere oke ha na ihe erimeeri ijuanya ma ọ bụ pụrụ iche, gụnyere ezi ọhịa, piikọkụ, ejula, na ụdị oke akpọrọ dormouse.
translations.reference: While most of their food would be familiar to us, Romans did have their share of strange or unusual feast items, including wild boar, peacock, snails, and a type of rodent called a dormouse
translations.hypothesis: Given the limited range of their diet, the Romans had a high preference for certain foods and delicacies, including wild boar, peacock, flamingo, and dormice.

translations.source: Ihe ọzọ dị iche bụ na ebe ndị ogbenye na nwanyị ahụ riri nri ha ka ha nọ ọdụ n'oche, ndị ọgaranya na-enwe mmasị inwe mmemme oriri ebe ha ga-eri nke ha n'ezumike.
translations.reference: Another difference was that while the poor people and the woman ate their food while sitting in chairs, the rich men liked to have banquets together where they would lounge on their sides while they ate their meals.
translations.hypothesis: Another distinction is that while the elderly couple ate their meals while sitting down, the rich man preferred to have his meals in a more formal setting.

translations.source: Ụmụ nri Ndị Rome Ndị mgbe ochie enwughị ike ịgụnye nri ndị batara Yurop site na Amerịka ma ọ bụ Eshịa na narị afọ ndị na-esotenu.
translations.reference: Ancient Roman meals couldn't have included foods that came to Europe from America or from Asia in later centuries.
translations.hypothesis: The ancient Roman diet was limited to foods grown in Europe or the Middle East.

translations.source: Na imaatu, ha enweghi oka, nweghi tomato, nweghi poteto, nweghi koko, na onweghi onye Rome mgbeochie deturu anu toro-toro ire.
translations.reference: For instance, they didn't have corn, nor tomatoes, nor potatoes, nor cocoa, and no ancient Roman ever tasted a turkey.
translations.hypothesis: In fact, they had no wheat, no tomatoes, no potatoes, no corn, and no one in Rome had ever seen a pineapple.

translations.source: Ndị Babịlọn rụrụ otu n’ime chi ha otu isi ụlọ nsọ nke e were ka ebe obibi chi ahụ.
translations.reference: The Babylonians built each of their gods a primary temple that was considered the home of the god.
translations.hypothesis: The Babylonians built a ziggurat to honor one of their gods as a place for the god to live.

translations.source: Ebe ndị mmadụ wetaara chi ndị ahụ aja, ndị nchụ aja ahụ maka ihe ha bụ chi na-achọ, site n'emume na mmemme di iche iche.
translations.reference: People would bring sacrifices to the gods and the priests would try to attend to the needs of the gods through ceremonies and festivals.
translations.hypothesis: Where people would bring their offerings to the shrine of the deity they wish to please, through various events and festivals.

translations.source: Ulo-uka n’otu n’otu nwere mbara-ezi ulo-uka ma nwekazie ime ebe nchuaja ebe nani onye-isi nchu-aja nwere-ike ibanye.
translations.reference: Each temple had an open temple courtyard and then an inner sanctuary that only the priests could enter.
translations.hypothesis: Each cell has a cell wall and also contains a cell membrane just inside the cell wall.

translations.source: Ụfọdụ oge a na arụnye ụlọ elu nwere oyiyi oiramid, ndị akpọrọ ziggurats, ka ha bụrụ osonye ụlọ okpukpe.
translations.reference: Sometimes special pyramid shaped towers, called ziggurats, were built to be a part of the temples.
translations.hypothesis: Sometimes a temple was built on top of a high tower, called a ziggurat, to make it closer to the gods.

translations.source: Elu ụlọ elu a bụ ebe dị nsọ pụrụ iche nye chi ahụ.
translations.reference: The top of the tower was special sanctuary for the god.
translations.hypothesis: The temple was a special place for the god.

translations.source: Na ekpem-oku nke udidi na mba ndi etiti owuwa-anyanwu, ulo ahu abachaghi uru.
translations.reference: In the warm climate of the Middle East, the house was not so important.
translations.hypothesis: In the cemetery of the Middle East, the building had long since collapsed.

translations.source: Ọtụtụ ihe ezinụlọ ndị juu a mere, ọ bụ n'anya onye ọbụla ka ha mere ya.
translations.reference: Most of the life of the Hebrew family happened in the open air.
translations.hypothesis: Many of the actions taken by high-income countries have been found to be detrimental to others.

translations.source: Ụmụ nwanyị siri nri na mbara eze; ụmụ ụlọ ahịa wụbụ naanị ọgụego mepere emepe na-elefe anya n'okporo ámá. E jire okwute maka ịrụ ụlọ.
translations.reference: Women did the cooking in the yard; stores were just open counters looking into the street. Stone was used for building houses.
translations.hypothesis: Women were in charge of food and the king's harem; the only open-air market was under their control. The buildings were made of stone.

translations.source: O nweghị ụmụ ọhịa buru ibu n’ala nke Keenan, ya mere osisi na-ada oke ọnụ.
translations.reference: There were no large forests in the land of Canaan, so wood was extremely expensive.
translations.hypothesis: There are no large game animals on the slopes of Mount Kenya, so the trees grow very tall.

translations.source: Ndị mmadụ anọjughị otu ebe na Grinland. N'akụkọ Norse ha sị na achụfuru Erik the Red n'obodo Iceland n'ihi igbu ọchụ, ma mgbe ọ na aga njem na mgbada ọdịda anyanwụ, ọchọpụtara Grinland wee gụọ ya Grinland.
translations.reference: Greenland was settled sparsely. In the Norse sagas they say that Erik the Red was exiled from Iceland for murder, and when travelling further west, found Greenland and named it Greenland.
translations.hypothesis: The people of Greenland did not settle the island. In Norse sagas it is said that Erik the Red was exiled from Iceland for murder, and while sailing west he discovered Greenland and named it thus.

translations.source: Mana n'agbanyeghi nchọpụta ya, agbụrụ Ezkimo ebirilarị ebe ahụ n'oge ahụ.
translations.reference: But regardless of his discovery, Eskimo tribes were already living there at the time.
translations.hypothesis: However, the discovery was made by an Inuit man.

translations.source: N'agbanyeghị na obodo ọbụla bụ 'mba Skandinevia', enwere ọtụtụ ihe dị iche n'etiti ndị, ndị eze, omenala, na akụkọ ihe mere na Denmak, Swiden, Nọọwe na Aisland.
translations.reference: Though each country was 'Scandinavian', there were many differences between the people, kings, customs and history of Denmark, Sweden, Norway and Iceland.
translations.hypothesis: Although every country is a Nordic country, there are many differences between the people, the languages, the cultures and the history of Denmark, Sweden, Norway and Iceland.

translations.source: Ọ bụrụ na ileela ihe nkiri a na-akpọ Akụ nke Mba, i nwere ike chee na e dere otu maapụ akụ n'azụ nke Nkwupụta nke Nnwere Onwe ahụ.
translations.reference: If you have watched the movie National Treasure, you may think a treasure map was written on the back of the Declaration of Independence.
translations.hypothesis: If you watch the movie "National Treasure", you might think that there is a literal treasure map behind the Declaration of Independence.

translations.source: Agbanyeghị, nke ahụ abụghị eziokwu. N’agbanyeghị na enwere ihe edere n’azụ nke dọkumentị ahụ, ọ bụghị otu maapụ akụ.
translations.reference: However, that is not true. Although there is something written on the back of the document, it is not a treasure map.
translations.hypothesis: However, that is not the case. Although there are documents behind the token, it is not a financial map.

translations.source: Ka-edere na azu nkwuputa nke nnoro-onwe bu okwua “Nkwuputa nke Nnoro-onwe Nke bu ezie ubochi abali 4 juli 1776” .Ederede ahu putara na ala-ala akwukwo ahu, kpodo isi na-ala.
translations.reference: Written on the back of the Declaration of Independence were the words "Original Declaration of Independence dated 4th July 1776". The text appears on the bottom of the document, upside down.
translations.hypothesis: The most famous of these is the United States Declaration of Independence, whose formal title is "The unanimous Declaration of the thirteen united States of America", and whose first sentence begins "When in the Course of human events...".

translations.source: Ọ bụ ezie na ọnweghị onye maara nke ọma onye dere ya, amaara na mmalite na ndụ ya, afụkọtara nnukwu dọkụment e jiri akpụkpọ anụ mee (o nwere nha inchì 29¾ site na inchì 24½) ọnụ maka nchekwa.
translations.reference: While no one knows for certain who wrote it, it is known that early in its life, the large parchment document (it measures 29¾ inches by 24½ inches) was rolled up for storage.
translations.hypothesis: Although the author is unknown, it is known that the original was a large document (29¾ by 24½ inches in size) which was chained for safekeeping.

translations.source: Ya mere, ọ dị ka agbakwụnyere ihe ngosi a dị ka akara njirimara naanị.
translations.reference: So, it is likely that the notation was added simply as a label.
translations.hypothesis: So, the show is just being presented as a standalone product.

translations.source: Ubochi-ubochi nladata ya agha ndi na esota atohapula mpaghara ugwu nke France, mana mpaghara ndida enwerebekwa onwe ha.
translations.reference: The D-Day landings and the following battles had freed the north of France, but the south still wasn't free.
translations.hypothesis: The regular army was defeated in the north of France, but the German command had a few independent formations.

translations.source: Ndị chịrị ya bụ ndị "Vichy" French. Ndị a bụ ndị mba Frans ndị ha na ndị mba Jamini mere udo n'afọ 1940 ma soro ndị iro rụkọọ ọrụ karịa ịlụso ha ọgụ.
translations.reference: It was ruled by the "Vichy" French. These were French people who had made peace with the Germans in 1940 and worked with the invaders instead of fighting them.
translations.hypothesis: Its leaders were the "Vichy" French. These were Frenchmen who had made a deal with the Jamaicans in the 1940s to work for the other side rather than fight.

translations.source: N'ụbọchị nke iri na ise nke ọnwa Ọgọọstụ n'afọ 1940, ndị enyi busoro mpaghara ndịda nke Frans agha, akpọrọ nke a "Operation Dragoon".
translations.reference: On 15 August 1940, the Allies invaded southern France, the invasion was called "Operation Dragoon".
translations.hypothesis: On August 15, 1944, the Allies launched an attack on the southern coast of France, called "Operation Dragoon".

translations.source: N'ime nanị izu abụọ ndị agha America na Ndị French nke Nweere onwe ha emeela ka ndịda France nwere onwe ha ma wee na-atụgharị echewe ihu na Germany.
translations.reference: In just two weeks the Americans and Free French forces had liberated southern France and were turning towards Germany.
translations.hypothesis: Within two weeks the American and French forces had liberated southern France and were poised to strike at Germany.

translations.source: Ọdịnala bụ otu omenaala ọha mmadụ buru ibu na-ebi ma na-arụkọ ọrụ ọnụ, a na-akpọ ọha mmadụ a sosayiti.
translations.reference: A civilization is a singular culture shared by a significant large group of people who live and work co-operatively, a society.
translations.hypothesis: A culture is a large social group that shares a geographic region, and to some extent a common culture.

translations.source: Ahịrịokwu "civilization" si n'okwu Latin bụ civilis, nke pụtara "gbasara obodo", nke metụtara okwu Latin bụ civis, nke pụtara onye obodo, na civitas, nke pụtara obodo maọbụ obodo-steeti, nke ahụ nwekwara otu o si egosi nha nke ọha mmadụ.
translations.reference: The word civilization comes from the Latin civilis, meaning civil, related to the Latin civis, meaning citizen, and civitas, meaning city or city-state, and that also somehow defines the size of the society.
translations.hypothesis: The word "civilization" comes from the Latin word civilis, which means "pertaining to a city", which derives from civis, meaning "citizen", and civitas, meaning "city" or "city-state", which also had the sense of "the people".

translations.source: Steeti-obodo gasị bụ obu ụzọ nke ụmụ mba. Omenaala kemmepeanya pụtara nnyefe nke ihe ọmụma n'etiti ọtụtụ ọgbọ, akaraụkwụ omenaala nke ka nọ ya na mgbasa dịtụ mma.
translations.reference: City-states are the precursors of nations. A civilizational culture implies the passing on of knowledge across several generations, a lingering cultural footprint and fair dissemination.
translations.hypothesis: States Parties are the primary means of implementing the Convention. Intangible cultural heritage refers to the transmission of knowledge, skills and meanings through generations, and is closely linked to the concept of sustainable development.

translations.source: Ụmụ obere ọdịnala na-apụ n'anya na-ahapụghị ihe akaebe dị mkpa ya mere anaghị ahụta ha dị ka sivilaịzeshọn kwesịrị ekwesị.
translations.reference: Minor cultures often vanish without leaving relevant historic evidence and fail to be recognized as proper civilizations.
translations.hypothesis: The few remaining small traditional cultures are often left with only a handful of living examples and are therefore not considered to be a proper civilization.

translations.source: Ka a na alụ agha ntụgharị, steeti iri na atọ ahụ bu ụzọ gbakọọ bido gọọmenti nchịkọta nke na adịghị ike - nke nzukọ bụ sọ ngalaba onwere- n'okpuru akwụkwọ obodo.
translations.reference: During the Revolutionary War, the thirteen states first formed a weak central government—with the Congress being its only component—under the Articles of Confederation.
translations.hypothesis: As the civil war dragged on, the thirteen colonies began to form a more formal government—a Continental Congress—under the Articles of Confederation.

translations.source: Nzukọ enweghị ike ike ụtụ ma n'ihi na enweghi ndị isi ọchịchị gọọmenti etiti maọbụ ndị omeiwu, ọ dabeere na ndị isi ọchịchị steeti, ndị anaghị enwe otu obi ọtụtụ oge ịkwado iwu ya nile.
translations.reference: Congress lacked any power to impose taxes, and, because there was no national executive or judiciary, it relied on state authorities, who were often uncooperative, to enforce all its acts.
translations.hypothesis: The legislature is weak and ineffective because it lacks the experience of central government and party politicians, and relies on state officials, who often pursue their own interests.

translations.source: O nweghi ikike imechi iwu ụtụisi na tarifu n'etiti steeti na steeti.
translations.reference: It also had no authority to override tax laws and tariffs between states.
translations.hypothesis: It does not have the power to impose taxes or duties between states.

translations.source: Ederede ahụ chọrọ nkweta steeti niile n'enweghi mgbagha tupu enwee ike imezi ha ma steeti ga weere gọọmentị etiti n'ihe efu ruo na ndị nnọchiteanya ha anaghị abịa.
translations.reference: The Articles required unanimous consent from all the states before they could be amended and states took the central government so lightly that their representatives were often absent.
translations.hypothesis: The text requires the unanimous consent of all States Parties before it can be amended and States Parties may not be bound by decisions taken by a majority of States Parties to which they have not given their consent.

translations.source: Ndị otu egwuregwu bọọlụ ukwu nke mba Itali, ya na ndị otu egwuregwu bọọlụ ukw nke mba Jamani bu ndị kacha eme nke ọma n'otu bọọlụ ukwu na mbaụwa ma bụrụkwa ndị nwetara mmeri n’iko mbaụwa nke afo 2006.
translations.reference: Italy's national football, along with German national football team is the second most successful team in the world and were the FIFA World Cup champions in 2006.
translations.hypothesis: The national association football teams of Italy and Germany are the most successful in the history of the sport, and were the finalists in the 2006 FIFA World Cup.

translations.source: Egwuregwu ndị a ma ama gụnyere futbọl, basketbọl, volleybọl, polo-mmiri, fencing, rugby, ịgba ịnyịnya, hockey ice, hockey roller na ịgba ọsọ ụgbọ ala F1.
translations.reference: Popular sports include football, basketball, volleyball, water-polo, fencing, rugby, cycling, ice hockey, roller hockey and F1 motor racing.
translations.hypothesis: Popular sports include soccer, basketball, volleyball, water polo, fencing, rugby, golf, ice hockey, roller hockey and Formula 1 auto racing.

translations.source: Egwuregwu oge oyi kachasị ewu ewu n'ugwu, ebe ndị mba Italy so asọ mpi n'egwuregwu mba na mba makwa na Olimpik.
translations.reference: Winter sports are most popular in the Northern regions, with Italians competing in international games and Olympic events.
translations.hypothesis: The most popular winter sport in the mountains, where Italy has always been a protagonist in the World Championships and the Olympics.

translations.source: Mba Japan nwere isuo ruru nde asaa (nke kachasị ibu bụ isuo Honshu), nke a mere mba Japan isuo nke asaa kacha ibu n'ụwa.
translations.reference: Japans holds nearly 7,000 islands (the biggest being Honshu), making Japan the 7th largest island in the world!
translations.hypothesis: Japan has 6,852 islands (the largest of which is Honshu), making it the country with the third-longest coastline in the world.

translations.source: N’ihi mkọkụlọta/òtù agwaetiti ahụ Japan nwere, a na-arụnyekarị Japan aka, n’elu etu ala ndị ahụ sị guzogide, dị ka "archipelago"
translations.reference: Due to the cluster/group of islands Japan has, Japan is often referred to, on a geographical stance, as an "archipelago"
translations.hypothesis: Due to Japan's unique island geography, Japan is often referred to as an "archipelago".

translations.source: Mbido mmepe Taịwan malitere n’oge gara aga nke narị afọ iri na ise mgbe ndị ọkwụ ụgbọ mmiri Ndị Yurop na-agafe dekọrọ aha agwaetiti ahụ dị ka Ilha Formosa, ma ọ bụ agwaetiti mara mma.
translations.reference: Taiwan beginning start way back in 15th century where European sailors passing by record the island’s name as Ilha Formosa, or beautiful island.
translations.hypothesis: The beginnings of the development of Taiwan go back to the fifteenth century when European sailors began to call the island Formosa, or Beautiful Island.

translations.source: N'afọ 1624, Ụlọọrụ Dọch Isti Indịa mepere ụlọọrụ na ndịda ọdịdaanyanwụ Taịwan, bido mgbanwe n'otu e si emepụta mkpụrụ n'oge gboo, ma wee ndị ọkpọkọọrụ Chaịna ka ha rụọ ọrụ n'ugbo osikapa na nke shuga ha.
translations.reference: In 1624,Dutch East India Company establishes a base in southwestern Taiwan, initiating a transformation in aboriginal grain production practices and employing Chinese laborers to work on its rice and sugar plantations.
translations.hypothesis: In 1624, the Dutch East India Company established a trading post in southwestern Taiwan, beginning a period of agricultural and commercial cooperation with the native Taiwanese and Chinese workers.

translations.source: N'afọ 1683, ndị agha ezinụlọ ọchịchị Shịng (1644-1912) weghaara akụkụ mmiri Taịwan dị n'ọdịda anyanwụ na nke dị n'ugwu ma kwuputa na Taịwan bụzi mpaghara n'okpuru ọchịchị Alaeze Shịng n'afọ 1885.
translations.reference: In 1683, Qing dynasty (1644-1912) forces take control of Taiwan’s western and northern coastal areas and declared Taiwan as a province of the Qing Empire in 1885.
translations.hypothesis: In 1683, the Qing Dynasty (1644–1912) militarily occupied Taiwan and formally declared it a prefecture of the Qing Empire in 1885.

translations.source: Na 1895, mgbe a dachara n’Agha Sino-Japanese Mbụ (1894-1895), ọchịchị Qing ahụ mere mbịanye aka na Nkwekọrịta nke Shimonoseki ahụ, site na nke o jiri nyefee Japan ọbụbụeze nke Taiwan, nke na-achị agwaetiti ahụ ruo 1945.
translations.reference: In 1895, after defeat in the First Sino-Japanese War (1894-1895), the Qing government signs the Treaty of Shimonoseki, by which it cedes sovereignty over Taiwan to Japan, which rules the island until 1945.
translations.hypothesis: In 1895, after losing the First Sino-Japanese War (1894–1895), the Qing government signed the Treaty of Shimonoseki, ceding Taiwan to Japan, which ruled the island until 1945.

translations.source: Machu Picchu nwere ọdịdị atọ, ya bụ Intihuatana, Ụlọ Nsọ nke Anyanwu, yana Ime ụlọ nke Windo Atọ.
translations.reference: Machu Picchu consist of three main structures, namely Intihuatana, the Temple of the Sun, and the Room of the Three Windows.
translations.hypothesis: Machu Picchu has three distinct features: the Intihuatana, the Temple of the Sun, and the Room of the Three Windows.

translations.source: Ọtụtụ n'ime ụlọ ndị nọ na mpụta ogige ụlọ ahụ ka arụgharịrị ka enwee ike gosi ndị njem nleta echiche etu ha siri pụta na mbụ.
translations.reference: Most of the buildings on the edges of the complex have been rebuilt in order to give tourists a better idea of how they originally appeared.
translations.hypothesis: Many of the buildings on the outer edge of the park have been reconstructed to give visitors an idea of what the area looked like in the past.

translations.source: Mgbe 1976 ruru, e mezigharịala pasent iri atọ nke Machu Pichu; mmezi a ka na-aga n'ihu ruo taa.
translations.reference: By 1976, thirty percent of Machu Picchu had been restored and restoration continues till today.
translations.hypothesis: By 1976, thirty percent of Machu Picchu had been rebuilt; this reconstruction continues to this day.

translations.source: Dịka ọmụmaatụ, nhàzi nka osise onyinyo nkwụ n'otu ebe a na-ahụkarị n'ụwa niile bụ 35mm, nke bụ nha fim kachasị ewu ewu na ngwụcha oge fim analọgụ.
translations.reference: For example, the most common still image photography format in the world is 35mm, which was the dominant film size at the close of the analog film era.
translations.hypothesis: For example, the standard focal length for a general-purpose zoom lens is 35mm, which is the most common film format.

translations.source: A ka na-emepụta ya taa, mana ihe ka mkpa bụ na ụdịdị sensọ foto nke igwefoto dijital eketala aspekt reshiyo ya.
translations.reference: It is still produced today, but more importantly its aspect ratio has been inherited by digital camera image sensor formats.
translations.hypothesis: It is still produced today, but more importantly, the photodetector array of digital cameras has evolved to the point where it surpasses the resolution of the human eye.

translations.source: Ọ dịtụ mgbagwoju anya na, n'ezie, ụdịdị 35mm nwere 36mm n'obosara na 24mm n'ogo.
translations.reference: The 35mm format is actually, somewhat confusingly, 36mm in width by 24mm in height.
translations.hypothesis: It is true that, technically, a 35mm negative is 36mm wide and 24mm high.

translations.source: akuku rashio nke usoro a ( iji iri na-abuo were nweta rashio onu ogugu dikasiri mfe) bu 3:2 maka nke a.
translations.reference: The aspect ratio of this format (dividing by twelve to obtain the simplest whole-number ratio) is therefore said to be 3:2.
translations.hypothesis: The aspect ratio of this format (using 16:9 for widescreen) is 3:2.

translations.source: Ọtụtụ usoro nkịtị (dịka usoro APS si n'otu ezinaụlọ) ga-abụ otu ihe maọbụ ruo ihe dịka nkepụta nkewa a.
translations.reference: Many common formats (APS family of formats, for example) are equal to or closely approximate this aspect ratio.
translations.hypothesis: Most common procedures (such as APS from the same family) will be similar or up to this standard.

translations.source: Iwu nke atọ ndị a na-akparị ma na-akwakarị oke emu bụ usoro dị mfe na-emepụta ịdịmgbanwò dị ka ọ na-edotekwa otu ụhara usoro ọrụ n'ime otu onyinyo.
translations.reference: The much-abused and often-ridiculed rule of thirds is a simple guideline creating dynamism while keeping a measure of order in an image.
translations.hypothesis: These three laws are a simple way to generate fractals that also mimic many natural phenomena in one fell swoop.

translations.source: O kwuru na ebe kachasị dị ire maka isi nke isiokwu bụ na mmekọta ụmụ ahịrị na-ekebi ụmụ onyinyo ahụ n’ụzọ atọ na nke eguzoro ọtọ nakwa nke a mara afọ n’ala (hụ ọmụmatụ).
translations.reference: It states that the most effective place for the main subject is at the intersection of lines dividing the image into thirds vertically and horizontally (see example).
translations.hypothesis: He said the most likely explanation for the odd appearance of the images is that the lines are caused by three or more stars lying along the same line of sight and being at different distances from Earth (see example).

translations.source: N'oge a na Yurop, e bidoro lebawa anya n'Ụka Katọlik, nke bagoro ụba ma dị ike.
translations.reference: During this period of European history, the Catholic Church, which had become rich and powerful, came under scrutiny.
translations.hypothesis: At this time in Europe, the Catholic Church had become very wealthy and powerful.

translations.source: Kamgbe ihe karịrị otu puku afọ, okpukpe Ndị Kraịst jikọtara obodo ndị dị na Yuropu n'agbanyeghị na asụsụ na omenala ha dịgasị iche.
translations.reference: For over a thousand years the Christian religion had bound European states together despite differences in language and customs. I
translations.hypothesis: For more than a thousand years, the Christian religion has helped to bind together the nations of Europe, despite their many and great differences of language and race.

translations.source: Ike ya juputara ebe niile metụtara onye ọbụla site n'eze ruo na mmadụ nkịtị.
translations.reference: Its all-pervading power affected everyone from king to commoner.
translations.hypothesis: Its influence is felt in every sphere of life, from the elite to the common man.

translations.source: Otu n'ime isi okwu okwukwe Ndị Kristian bu na ekwesiri iji akụ belata nhụjuanya na ịda ogbenye nakwa na ego ụka nọ kpọmkwem ebe ahụ n'ihi nke ahụ.
translations.reference: One of the main Christian tenets is that wealth should be used to alleviate suffering and poverty and that the monetary funds of the church are there specifically for that reason.
translations.hypothesis: One of the main points of Christian doctrine is that poverty and suffering are due to greed and the unequal distribution of wealth.

translations.source: Ikike keetiti ahụ nke ụlọ uka anọọla n'ime Rom karịa otu puku afọ ma mkpọkọnata ike na ego a duru ọtụtụ ndị ịjụ sị ma a na-esokwa ụkpụrụ ya.
translations.reference: The central authority of the church had been in Rome for over a thousand years and this concentration of power and money led many to question whether this tenet was being met.
translations.hypothesis: The four main churches of Rome have existed for over a thousand years and the power and influence they have had has led to many inquisitions and the persecution of heretics.

translations.source: Ka agha dara, mba Britenị jiri ndị agha elu mmiri gbochie ndị Jamani inweta enyemaka
translations.reference: Soon after the outbreak of hostilities, Britain initiated a naval blockade of Germany.
translations.hypothesis: As the war went on, the Royal Navy blockaded Germany to stop them getting supplies.

translations.source: Atụmatụ ahụ rụrụ ọrụ ọfụma, na-ebepụ ụmụ ihe mbute ihe ndị agha na ndị nkiti dị oke mpka, n’agbanyeghị na mgbochi a dara iwu mba ụwa anabatara n’izugbe nke ọtụtụ nkwekọrịta n’etiti mba ụwa nke afọ narị abụọ gara aga nyere ikikere.
translations.reference: The strategy proved effective, cutting off vital military and civilian supplies, although this blockade violated generally accepted international law codified by several international agreements of the past two centuries.
translations.hypothesis: The plan worked well, neutralizing the most dangerous of the materials, though the ban on international trade in these materials has been undermined in recent years by a series of bilateral agreements.

translations.source: Briten tinyere ogbunigwe na mmiri ọha mba igbochi ụgbọ mmiri ọbụla ịbata, nke a abụrụ ihe ize ndụ nye ụgbọ mmiri ndị esoghi alụ agha.
translations.reference: Britain mined international waters to prevent any ships from entering entire sections of ocean, causing danger to even neutral ships.
translations.hypothesis: Britain also mined the approaches to the harbour, which made it dangerous for any ships to enter.

translations.source: Ebe nzaghachi ihe omume a pere mpe, mba Jamini lere anya na a ga emekwa otu ihe n'ebe agha okpuru mmiri nọ.
translations.reference: Since there was limited response to this tactic, Germany expected a similar response to its unrestricted submarine warfare.
translations.hypothesis: Given the ambiguous nature of the response, Jamaica is unlikely to take any action regarding the undersea cable.

translations.source: N'oge afọ ndi 1920, agwa kachasị dị ebe nile n'etiti ndị mba dị iche iche bụ nke ịchọ udo na nnọrọ onwe.
translations.reference: During the 1920s, the prevailing attitudes of most citizens and nations was that of pacifism and isolation.
translations.hypothesis: In the 1920s, the most common attitude toward immigration among the general public in many countries was one of tolerance and acceptance.

translations.source: Mgbe a hụchara ụmụ egwu na ajọ ọmụme nke agha n’oge Agha Ụwa I, mba gasị chọrọ izere ụdị ọnọdụ ahụ ọzọ n’ọdịnihu.
translations.reference: After seeing the horrors and atrocities of war during World War I, nations desired to avoid such a situation again in the future.
translations.hypothesis: After the use of poison gas in World War I, countries sought to ban the use of such weapons in the future.

translations.source: N'afọ 1884, Tesla kwagara na mba Amerịka ịnara ọrụ na nke Ụlọ ọrụ Edison n'Obodo Niu Yọk.
translations.reference: In 1884, Tesla moved to the United States of America to accept a job with the Edison Company in New York City.
translations.hypothesis: In 1884, Tesla emigrated to the United States to work for the Edison Company in New York City.

translations.source: Ọ bịarutere na US n’inwe centị anọ n’aha ya, otu akwụkwọ nke uri, ya na otu akwụkwọ ozi nke nkwanye sitere na Charles Batchelor (onye njikwa ya n’ọrụ ya gara aga) ruo Thomas Edison.
translations.reference: He arrived in the US with 4 cents to his name, a book of poetry, and a letter of recommendation from Charles Batchelor (his manager in his previous job) to Thomas Edison.
translations.hypothesis: It included four cents in US currency, a copy of the poem, and a letter of introduction from Charles Batchelor (a former employer) to Thomas Edison.

translations.source: Chaịna ndị mgbe ochie nwere ụzọ pụrụ iche igosi oge afọ; ogo ọbụla nke Chaịna ma ọ bụ ezinụlọ ọ bụla nọbụrụ n’ọchịchị wụbụ oge ọchịchị eze pụrụ iche.
translations.reference: Ancient China had a unique way of showing different time periods; each stage of China or each family that was in power was a distinctive dynasty.
translations.hypothesis: Ancient China had a unique way of marking the passage of time; each Chinese dynasty or clan ruled for a certain number of years.

translations.source: Nakwa n’etiti usoro ndị eze ọ bụla bụ otu oge ejighị n'aka mke mpaghara ndị kewara ekewa. Oge ndị a nke a kacha mara amara bụ oge nke Alaeze Atọ nke mere ruo afọ iri na isii n'etiti Usoro Ndị Eze Han na Usoro Ndị Eze Jin ndị ahụ.
translations.reference: Also between each dynasty was an unstable age of divided provinces. The best-known of these periods was the Three Kingdoms epoch taking place for 60 years between the Han and the Jin Dynasty.
translations.hypothesis: Also within each of these imperial cycles there was a period of disunity. The most famous of these periods is the Three Kingdoms period which occurred during the late Han Dynasty and the early Jin Dynasty.

translations.source: N'oge ndị a, a lụrụ ọtụtụ agha n'etiti ndi ukwu na-azọ oche eze.
translations.reference: During these periods fierce warfare took place between many nobles fighting for the throne.
translations.hypothesis: During this time, there were many wars between the kings.

translations.source: Alaeze Atọ so n'otu n'ime ọgbọ kacha dị egwu n'akụkọ ihe mere na mba Chaịna mgbe gboo. Puku kwuru puku mmadụ nwụrụ n'agha ịnọ n'oche ọchịchị nke kachasị elu na nnukwu obi eze nke dị na Xi'an.
translations.reference: The Three Kingdoms was one of the bloodiest eras in Ancient China’s history thousands of people died fighting to sit in the highest seat in the grand palace at Xi’an.
translations.hypothesis: The Three Kingdoms is one of the most romanticized periods in Chinese history. Tens of thousands of people died in battles for the highest office in the largest empire in the world, the Imperial Court of the Great Han Dynasty, which was based in the ancient capital of Xi'an.

translations.source: Nke a butere ọtụtụ mmetụta na mmekọ mmadụ na ibe ya makwa na ndọrọ ndọrọ ọchịchị dika usoro agụm ọnụ, mgbanwe site n'ọchịchị okwu otu onye gaa na nke okwu mba, nke obodo na nkwenye na obodo bụ nke ọha karịa ịbụ nke otu onye ọchịchị.
translations.reference: There are a lot of social and political effects such as the use of metric system, a shift from absolutism to republicanism, nationalism and the belief the country belongs to the people not to one sole ruler.
translations.hypothesis: This has had many impacts on social and political organization including the development of money, the shift from autocratic to democratic forms of government, and the concept of the nation-state and the popular sovereignty.

translations.source: Ọzọkwa mgbe ụmụ aka ọrụ Mgbanwe ọchịchị ahụ mepechara maka ụmụ nwoke ọchọ ọrụ niile na-ekwe ka ndị kacha nwee oké ọchịchọ na ihe ịga nke ọma ka ha gaa nke ọma.
translations.reference: Also after the Revolution occupations were open to all male applicants allowing the most ambitious and successful to succeed.
translations.hypothesis: Moreover, when the military junta opened up the country to foreign job agencies, only the most desperate and unqualified job seekers were left behind.

translations.source: Ọ bụkwa otu ihe ahụ n'amị, maka na kama nhazi n'usoro nke ndị amị ga-adabere n'ogugo, ọ daberezie n'ikikere.
translations.reference: Same goes for the military because instead of army rankings being based on class they were now based on cailaber.
translations.hypothesis: It is also the case in the ear, for while the order of the bones in the middle ear is determined by the need to amplify the sound, the shape of the outer ear is determined by the need to localize sounds.

translations.source: Mgbanwe France melitere obi ndi oru ana emegbu emegbu no gasi na mba ndi ozo ha ewere wee ike ibido mgbanwe nke ha.
translations.reference: The French Revolution also inspired many other repressed working class people of other country's to began their own revolutions.
translations.hypothesis: French reforms have raised the hopes of workers in other countries who want to bring about similar changes.

translations.source: Muhammad nwere ezigbo mmasị n’ụmụ okwu gabigara ụwa a na-agwụ ike. Ọ dịbụ na-agakarị n’otu nnukwu ọnụala nke emechara mara dị ka “Hira‘” n’ugwu nke “Noor” (light) maka ntụgharị ụche.
translations.reference: Muhammad was deeply interested in matters beyond this mundane life. He used to frequent a cave that became known as “Hira‘” on the Mountain of “Noor” (light) for contemplation.
translations.hypothesis: Muhammad had a great interest in the esoteric aspects of Islam. He often went to a remote mountain shrine known as the "Hira' Gully" (the gully of Hira) for meditation.

translations.source: ọgba ahụ n'onwe ya, nke lanarịrị oge ndị a, na-enye ezigbo ihe ngosi maka echiche gbasara ihe mmụọ nke Muhammad.
translations.reference: he cave itself, which survived the times, gives a very vivid image of Muhammad’s spiritual inclinations.
translations.hypothesis: The Dome of the Rock, in particular, provides a stunning visual representation of Islamic artistic and architectural concepts.

translations.source: Na-ezu ike n’elu otu n’ime ugwu ndị nọ n’uwgu nke Meeka, nnukwu ọnụala dịpụrụ adịpụ n’ozuzu site n’akụkụ ụwa ndị ọzọ niile
translations.reference: Resting on the top of one of the mountains north of Mecca, the cave is completely isolated from the rest of the world.
translations.hypothesis: Towering over the surrounding landscape, the peak of Mauna Kea is the highest point in the world when measured from base to summit.

translations.source: N'ezie, ọ dịghị mfe maọlị ịchọta, ọbụrụgodi na mmadụ maara na ọ dị. Ozugbo abanyere n'ime ọgba ahụ, ọ bụ ndịpụ kpam kpam.
translations.reference: In fact, it is not easy to find at all even if one knew it existed. Once inside the cave, it is a total isolation.
translations.hypothesis: In fact, it is not easy to find, even if you know where to look. Once inside the cave, it is a steep and slippery descent.

translations.source: O nweghị ihe ọzọ enwere ike ịhụ na-abụghị eluigwe dị n’elu gbachapụrụ, maa mma na ọtụtụ ugwu gbara gburugburu. Nanị obere nke ụwa ka enwere ike ịhụ ma ọ bụ nụ site n’ime nnukwu ọnụala ahụ.
translations.reference: Nothing can be seen other than the clear, beautiful sky above and the many surrounding mountains. Very little of this world can be seen or heard from inside the cave.
translations.hypothesis: There was nothing to see but the sky above, a brilliant blue, and the surrounding cliffs. The only sounds were the wind and the distant rush of water.

translations.source: Oke Piramid na Giza bụ naanị nke ka kwụ taa n'ime ihe itụnanya asaa ahụ.
translations.reference: The Great Pyramid at Giza is the only one of the seven wonders that is still standing today.
translations.hypothesis: The Great Pyramid of Giza is the only one of the original Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing.

translations.source: Ndị Ijipt rụrụ n’ime narị afọ atọ BCE, Oke Piramidi ahụ otu n’ime ọtụtụ nnukwu ihe ọwụwụ piramidi arụrụ ịkwanye Fero nwụrụ ugwu.
translations.reference: Built by the Egyptians in the third century BCE, the Great Pyramid is one of many large pyramid structures built to honor dead Pharaoh.
translations.hypothesis: Built during the Third Dynasty BCE, the Step Pyramid of Djoser is the earliest complete stone building complex in Egypt.

translations.source: Ala ugwu Giza maọbụ "Giza Nekropolis" nke dị na ndagwurugwu ọnwụ Ijipt nwere ọtụtụ piramid (nke piramid ukwu bụ nke kachasị ibu), ọtụtụ ebe olili, ọtụtụ ụlọ ofufe nakwa oke Sfinks.
translations.reference: The Giza Plateau, or "Giza Necropolis" in the Egyptian Valley of the Dead contains several pyramids (of which the great pyramid is the largest), several small tombs, several temples, and the great Sphinx.
translations.hypothesis: The Giza Plateau or "Giza Necropolis" is located on the Giza Plateau in Egypt and consists of three main pyramids (the largest of which is the Great Pyramid), several smaller pyramids, numerous tombs, and the Great Sphinx.

translations.source: Arụrụ oke piramid iji kwanyere Eze Khufu zugwu, ya na ọtụtụ piramid obere ndị ọzọ, ebe olili na ụlọ ofufe arụrụ ịkwanyere ndị inyom Khufu na ezinụlọ ya ugwu.
translations.reference: The great pyramid was created to honor the Pharaoh Khufu, and many of the smaller pyramids, tombs, and temples were built to honor Khufu's wives and family members.
translations.hypothesis: The Great Pyramid was built to house the tomb of the pharaoh Khufu, and several smaller pyramids, temples and tombs were built to house the wives, children and other family members of Khufu.

translations.source: Akara “ụta elu” ahụ yiri otu V ma akara “ụta ala” ahụ yiri otu stepụlụ ma ọ bụ otu ǹkomgbaànoǹhà nke tufure ebe okpuru ya.
translations.reference: The "up bow" mark looks like a V and the "down bow mark" like a staple or a square missing its bottom side.
translations.hypothesis: The upstroke of the letter V and the downstroke of the letter A are combined into one continuous stroke, and the bottom of the A is extended to form the crossbar.

translations.source: Elu pụtara na Ị kwesịrị isi n'ọnụnụ ya pịa ụta aka, ma ala pụtara na Ị kwesịrị isi na fụrọgụ (nke bụ ebe aka gị ji ụta) were dọọ ụta aka.
translations.reference: Up means you should start at the tip and push the bow, and down means you should start at the frog (which is where your hand is holding the bow) and pull the bow.
translations.hypothesis: The knuckle is the part of the hand you hit with your fingers, and the palm is the part of your hand you hit with the back of your fingers.

translations.source: Otu ụta-elu na -emepụtakarị ụda kara dị nro, ebe ụta-ala ka sie ike ma kara kwupụta.
translations.reference: An up-bow usually generates a softer sound, while a down-bow is stronger and more assertive.
translations.hypothesis: The higher-pitched sounds are usually softer, while the lower-pitched sounds are louder and more emphasized.

translations.source: Detuo akara nke gị na nwere onwe, mana chetakwa na akara ndị ahụ ebiri ebi nwere uru egwu ha bara, n'ihi nke a ha kwesịrị ka akwanyere ha ugwu.
translations.reference: Feel free to pencil in your own marks, but remember the printed bowing marks are there for a musical reason, so they should usually be respected.
translations.hypothesis: Make your own mark, but also respect the existing graffiti, as some of it is valuable art and should be preserved.

translations.source: N'Oktoba 6, 1789, ụmụ nwanyị ahịa iwe ji yiri Eze Luwi XVI oke egwu mgbe ha si na Versailles dọrọ ya, nwunye ya Marịa Antwanet, obere ụmụ ha abụọ (Marịa Teriza dị afọ 11 na Luwi-Chals dị afọ anọ), na nwanne nwanyị Eze, Madam Elizabet, dọghachi ha na Parii.
translations.reference: The terrified King Louis XVI, Queen Marie Antoinette their two young children (11 year old Marie Therese and four year old Louis-Charles) and the King's sister, Madam Elizabeth, on the 6th October 1789 were forced back to Paris from Versailles by a mob of market women.
translations.hypothesis: On October 6, 1789, a hostile mob of women marched from Versailles to Paris, where they were joined by the King, his wife Marie Antoinette, their two children (11-year-old Marie Thérèse and four-year-old Louis-Charles), and the King's sister, Madame Elisabeth.

translations.source: Ha laghachiri Paris n'ime moto ịnyịnya ndị iwe na-ewe gbara gburugburu, ha na-eti mkpu na-agwa Eze na Nwunye ya ihe egwu dị iche iche.
translations.reference: In a carriage, they traveled back to Paris surrounded by a mob of people screaming and shouting threats against the King and Queen.
translations.hypothesis: They returned to Paris in a motorcade surrounded by police, warning the King and Queen of the many threats against their lives.

translations.source: Ndị iwe a manyere Eze na Queen ka ha meghee windo ụgbọ ha.
translations.reference: The mob of people forced the King And Queen to have their carriage windows wide open.
translations.hypothesis: The protesters demanded that the King and Queen open the doors of their carriage.

translations.source: N'otu mgbe otu n'ime ndị igwe mmadụ fegharịrị isi onye nche eze egburu na Versailles n'ihu eze nwanyi ụjọ ji.
translations.reference: At one point a member of the mob waved the head of a royal guard killed at Versailles in front of the terrified Queen.
translations.hypothesis: At one point a soldier fired a shot at the Queen's guard and missed.

translations.source: Mmefu ego n'agha nke ndị Amerịka mbịarachịwa na mmeri ndị Filipaị bụ nke ndị Filipino kwụrụ ụgwọ ya n’onwe ha.
translations.reference: The war expenditures of U.S. imperialism in the conquest of the Philippines were paid for by the Filipino people themselves.
translations.hypothesis: The cost of the American war of aggression and the subsequent Filipino victory was paid for by the Filipino people themselves.

translations.source: A manyere ha iwu ịkwụ ụtụisi nye ndị ọchịchị mbịarachịwa mba Amerịka iji wedata oke ego e mefuru n'aha gọọmenti mba Filipin site n'aka ụlọakụ Wọlụ Striti.
translations.reference: They were compelled to pay taxes to the U.S. colonial regime to defray a major part of the expenditures and the interest on bonds floated in the name of the Philippine government through the Wall Street banking houses.
translations.hypothesis: They were ordered to pay the US government $1.7 million in restitution for defrauding the Philippine government of the funds through the Wolseley Street branch of the bank.

translations.source: N’eziokwu, nnukwu uru e nwetara na ogologo mmegbu ndị mba Filipiinụ ga-abụ ihe mejuputara isi uru omume empaya Amerịka.
translations.reference: Of course, the superprofits derived from the protracted exploitation of the Filipino people would constitute the basic gains of U.S. imperialism.
translations.hypothesis: In fact, the great benefit to the Philippines of this American imperialism was the realization of the American dream.

translations.source: Ịghọta ndị Templars, aghaghi ịghọta ọnọdụ nke kpaliri okike nke otu a.
translations.reference: To understand the Templars one must understand the context that prompted the creation of the order.
translations.hypothesis: To understand the Templars, you must first understand the conditions that led to the formation of the order.

translations.source: Ọgbọ ihe ndị a mere na ya ka a na-akpọkarị Ọgbọ Etiti dị Elu bụ oge ihe ndị mere na mba Yuropu n'afọ narị iri na otu, narị iri na abụọ na narị iri na atọ (AD 1000-1300).
translations.reference: The age where the events took place is commonly referred as the High Middle Ages the period of European history in the 11th, 12th, and 13th centuries (AD 1000–1300).
translations.hypothesis: The period is often referred to as the High Middle Ages and lasted from about 1000 to 1300 AD.

translations.source: Ọgbọ etiti ndị nke mbụ butere ọgbọ etiti ndị dị elu ụzọ, nke ọgbọ etiti nke ngwụcha sotere n'azụ nke gwuru ebe 1500.
translations.reference: The High Middle Ages were preceded by the Early Middle Ages and followed by the Late Middle Ages, which by convention ends around 1500.
translations.hypothesis: The first half of the 19th century produced a boom in the construction of high-level roads, and the second half saw the construction of over 1500 bridges.

translations.source: Mkpebi teknụụzụ bụ usoro gazuru nchịkọta nchepụta gasị etinyere n’uju, site na technụụzụ-kwàa maọbụ nye iwu siri ike nke bụ na njedebe nke onye ga-esite n’iwu metụtara sayensi na nke ngosipụta teknụụzụ.
translations.reference: Technological determinism is a term that encompasses a wide range of ideas in practice, from technology-push or the technological imperative to a strict sense that human destiny is driven by an underlying logic associated with scientific laws and their manifestation in technology.
translations.hypothesis: A technology regulation is a process that goes beyond the collection of data and is based on a technology-neutral or technologically neutral rule that is independent of the scientific or technical state of the art.

translations.source: Ọtụtụ nkọwa e nyere nkwenyesiike kenkanụzụ nwere echiche izugbe abụọ: na mmepụta nkanụzụ n'onwe ya na-agbaso usoro nke gbapụrụ iche site na nkwanye nke omenala maọbụ ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị, ya na kwa na nkanụzụ n'aka nke ya nwere "mmekpaahụ" ọ na-enye ọhaobodo nke dị adị, n'abụghị nke sitere na mmekọrịta.
translations.reference: Most interpretations of technological determinism share two general ideas: that the development of technology itself follows a path largely beyond cultural or political influence, and that technology in turn has "effects" on societies that are inherent, rather than socially conditioned.
translations.hypothesis: Many definitions of consent include two key elements: consent must be given freely, without coercion or manipulation, and consent must be informed, meaning that the person giving consent understands what they are consenting to.

translations.source: Maka ọmụmaatụ, mmadụ nwere ike ịsị na ụgbọala n'ịkwesị ekwesị na-eduga na mmepe nke ụzọ gasị.
translations.reference: For example, one might say that the motor car necessarily leads to the development of roads.
translations.hypothesis: For example, people may be more inclined to cycle if there are cycle lanes.

translations.source: N'agbanyeghị nke a, okporo ụzọ zuru obodo ọnụ bụ mmefu ego ma ọbụrụ na ụgbọ ala ehighị nne, ya mere emepụtara ụzọ ọhụrụ ịwedata ego o na ewe inwe ụgbọala.
translations.reference: However, a nationwide road network is not economically viable for just a handful of cars, so new methods of production are developed to reduce the cost of car ownership.
translations.hypothesis: However, the city's roads are expensive to drive on, so an alternative was developed to allow people to own cars without driving them on public roads.

translations.source: Ọtụtụ mmadụ inwe ụgbọ ala na-ebutekwa nnukwu ihe mberede n'okporo ụzọ, nke na-eweta mmepụta usoro nleta ahụike ọhụrụ maka ịrụzi ahụ mebiri emebi.
translations.reference: Mass car ownership also leads to a higher incidence of accidents on the roads, which leads to the invention of new techniques in healthcare for repairing damaged bodies.
translations.hypothesis: The increasing motorization of transport also contributes to traffic accidents, which in turn increase the need for specialized medical services to treat the resulting injuries.

translations.source: Ihunanya ya nwere otutu ihe banyere mmeme nke ọdịnala, nke sitere n'aka ndị edemede dịka Goethe, Fichte, na Schlegel.
translations.reference: Romanticism had a large element of cultural determinism, drawn from writers such as Goethe, Fichte, and Schlegel.
translations.hypothesis: His aestheticism had much to do with the cultural movement of the time, influenced by writers such as Goethe, Fichte, and Schlegel.

translations.source: Na onodu romanticism, ala ebe onye no bu ihe na kpu omume mmadu, k’oge na aga odinala na omenala metutara ala ebe obibi amalite, nkea mere ndi mmadu jiri nabata odinala na omenala ndia maka na ha na ya bu odinala na omenala nwere nkwekorita karia iwu ana atukwasa n’isi oha.
translations.reference: In the context of Romanticism, the geography molded individuals, and over time customs and culture related to that geography arose, and these, being in harmony with the place of the society, were better than arbitrarily imposed laws.
translations.hypothesis: With Romanticism, the homeland became the central theme of artistic expression, and the folk culture and traditions of the homeland were idealized, so that people could identify with the nation and its ideals, which were often more abstract than the state's legal code.

translations.source: N'otu aka a maara Paris ka isi ejiji ịchọ mma n'ụwa nke oge a, e weere Kọnstantinopul dịka isi ejiji ịchọ mma na mba Yuropu n'oge agha.
translations.reference: In the manner that Paris is known as the fashion capital of the contemporary world, Constantinople was regarded as the fashion capital of feudal Europe.
translations.hypothesis: While Paris is known as the fashion capital of the world today, Constantinople was considered the height of fashion in Europe at the time of the crusades.

translations.source: Ebidoro n’afo 400A.D. ruo n’afo 1100 A.D were mara ya na o bu isi mkporindu.
translations.reference: Its renown for being an epicenter of luxury began in about 400 A.D. and lasted up until about 1100 A.D.
translations.hypothesis: It was established between 400 A.D. to 1100 A.D. and was known to be a major producer.

translations.source: Ọkwa na gbadara n’oge narị afọ iri na abụọ tụmadị n’ihi eziokwu bụ na Ndị agha ntute alaghachila ma bute ụmụ onyinye dị ka ụmụ akwa sịlk na ngwa nri ndị nwere mbamuru karịrị ihe ahịa Byzantine nyere.
translations.reference: Its status declined during the twelfth century mainly due to the fact that Crusaders had returned bearing gifts such as silks and spices that were valued more than what Byzantine markets offered.
translations.hypothesis: The quality declined during the 12th century, mainly because the Crusaders destroyed many of the workshops and the silk and food production was taken over by the Venetians.

translations.source: Ọ bụ n'oge ahụ ka okwa isi ejiji ịchọ ma siri na Kọnstantinopul fere Paris.
translations.reference: It was at this time that the transfer of the title of Fashion Capital from Constantinople to Paris was made.
translations.hypothesis: It was then that the idea of a head-to-head duel between the two champions began to take shape in Constantinople and Paris.

translations.source: Usoro Gotik kasị elu n'oge dị n'etiti afọ ndị nari nke ir na narị nke iri na otu ya na narị nke iri na anọ.
translations.reference: Gothic style peaked in the period between the 10th - 11th centuries and the 14th century.
translations.hypothesis: The peak of Gothic style was in the mid-12th and early 13th centuries.

translations.source: Na mbido, ọ bụ usoro ejiji ndị Byzantium n'ọwụwa anyanwụ ka onye ọbụla na-eso.
translations.reference: At the beginning dress was heavily influenced by the Byzantine culture in the east.
translations.hypothesis: Initially, it was the Byzantine court's fashions that everyone tried to follow.

translations.source: Mana, n'ihi ụkpụrụ mkparịta ụka na adịghị ọsịsọ, usoro dị na ọdịda anyanwụ nwere ike inọzụga azụ n'oteaka afọ iri abụọ na ise ruo iri atọ.
translations.reference: However, due to the slow communication channels, styles in the west could lag behind by 25 to 30 year.
translations.hypothesis: However, because of the slower pace of conversation, a sunset cruise can last anywhere from twenty to thirty years.

translations.source: na njedebe nke oge Mịdụl Eeji ndị ọdịda anyanwụ Europe malitere mepụtawa usoro nke ha. Otu ihe mmepụta kachasi mkpa n'oge ahụ, n'ihi ọgụ aghara, ndị mmadụ bidoro iji bọtịnụ akpọchị akwa.
translations.reference: towards the end of the Middle Ages western Europe began to develop their own style. one of the biggest developments of the time as a result of the crusades people began to use buttons to fasten clothing.
translations.hypothesis: In the Middle Ages European tailors began to develop their own styles. The most important development of the time, due to the Crusades, was the introduction of the button.

translations.source: Ugbo oru bu ihe oru ugbo bu nke eweputara iji meputa nri ga ezuru ndi mmadu choro ya ma obu ya na ulo ya.
translations.reference: Subsistence agriculture is agriculture carried out for the production of enough food to meet just the needs of the agriculturalist and his/her family.
translations.hypothesis: Farming is the practice of cultivating plants and rearing animals to provide food for humans and themselves.

translations.source: Ịkọ ọrụ ugbo bụ ihe dịcha mfe, ọtụtụ mgbe nke ndụ, sistèm n'iji nkpụrụ echekwara bụ nwa afọ na mphaghara ebe obibi ahụ ejikọtara ya na nghagharị mkpụrụ ma ọ bụ usoro ndị ọzọ dị mfe iji mee ka ọmịmị kachasị.
translations.reference: Subsistence agriculture is a simple, often organic, system using saved seed native to the ecoregion combined with crop rotation or other relatively simple techniques to maximize yield.
translations.hypothesis: Farming is a relatively simple, often lifelong, system that uses stored energy in the form of seeds and is closely linked to the local environment and simple technologies to produce food.

translations.source: Na mgbe gboo ọtụtụ n'ime ndị na-akọ ugbo na-eme ụdị nke onwe n'enweghị nke orire ọ ka dịkwa otu a n'ọtụtụ obodo ka na etolite etolite.
translations.reference: Historically most farmers were engaged in subsistence agriculture and this is still the case in many developing nations.
translations.hypothesis: And while many farmers still produce on a small scale, there are also commercial farms in many countries.

translations.source: Obere omenaala na-ekpọkọta ọnụ ndị nwere ụdị echiche ndị nwere mmetụta na ụkpụrụ keobodo ha leghaara ha anya ma nye ha ohere ịzụlite echiche nke njirimara.
translations.reference: Subcultures bring together like-minded individuals who feel neglected by societal standards and allow them to develop a sense of identity.
translations.hypothesis: Small groups tend to attract people with similar interests and values, and allow for the development of a sense of identity.

translations.source: Enwere ike imata ngalaba omenala site na afo, agburu, klaasi, ebe onye bi, ma o bu etu chukwu si kee mmadu -i bu nwoke ka ibu nwanyi.
translations.reference: Subcultures can be distinctive because of the age, ethnicity, class, location, and/or gender of the members.
translations.hypothesis: Cultural dimensions can be categorized by age, gender, ethnicity, geographic region, and socioeconomic status.

translations.source: Ihe nlereanya aji ama na omenala pụrụ iche bụ asụsụ, ịchọ mma, okpukpe, ọchịchị, mmekọahụ, ọnọdụ ebe, maọbu njikọ ọtụtụ ihe.
translations.reference: The qualities that determine a subculture as distinct may be linguistic, aesthetic, religious, political, sexual, geographical, or a combination of factors.
translations.hypothesis: Typical cultural elements are language, arts, religion, cuisine, politics, sexuality, and gender, among others.

translations.source: Ndịòtù nke otu okpuru omenala na-akpọtụrụkarị ịdị n'òtù ha site n'otu ojiji akanka pụrụ iche ma dịmara, nke gụnyere ụmụ ejiji, omume, na asụsụ ịgba izu.
translations.reference: Members of a subculture often signal their membership through a distinctive and symbolic use of style, which includes fashions, mannerisms, and argot.
translations.hypothesis: Subcultures are often defined by a particular style of dress, behaviour and speech, which sets them apart from the mainstream culture.

translations.source: Otu n’ime ukpuru akacha mara nke atuzi-aka banyere uru di mmekorita bu iweta n’uche ihe nwute banyere umu-aka ndi elefuuru-anya, na-nwuta, maobu mmeto akpachaara-anya mee, enweghi mmekorita ha ndi toro-eto mgbe ha ka na-eto eto.
translations.reference: One of the most common methods used to illustrate the importance of socialization is to draw upon the few unfortunate cases of children who were, through neglect, misfortune, or wilful abuse, not socialized by adults while they were growing up.
translations.hypothesis: One of the most common misconceptions about the benefits of assisted reproduction is the belief that it is only useful for older couples who have difficulty conceiving.

translations.source: Ụdị ụmụaka a ka a na akpọ ndị azụghị azụ. Ọtụtụ ụmụaka an na azụghị azụ abụrụla ndị ndị mmadụ jituru ejitu (ọ na abụkarị ndị mụrụ ha); oge ụfọdụ ngharịpụ ụmụaka bụ maka ọjụjụ ntụpọ dị na ahụ nwatakịrị ahụ a na ahụ anya maọbụ ntụpọ dị n' akọ n'uche ya.
translations.reference: Such children are called "feral" or wild. Some feral children have been confined by people (usually their own parents); in some cases this child abandonment was due to the parents' rejection of a child's severe intellectual or physical impairment.
translations.hypothesis: These children are sometimes referred to as abandoned children. Many such children are taken in by relatives (usually the closest relatives); in some cases the adoption is open and the biological parents are known, but sometimes the adoption is closed and the child never learns the identity of his or her biological parents.

translations.source: Ụmụaka azụghịazụ nwere ike ha e nweela ahụmihe nke mmetọ ụmụaka ma ọ bụ ahụmihe mkpasasị uche nke ukwuu tupu agbahapụ ha ma ọ bụ ha na-agbalaga.
translations.reference: Feral children may have experienced severe child abuse or trauma before being abandoned or running away.
translations.hypothesis: Children who are adopted may have a history of abuse or severe emotional trauma before they are adopted.

translations.source: Ndị ọzọ bụ ebubo ka eboro n’ọbụ ụmụ anụmanụ kpọpụtara ha; a sịkwara n’ụfọdụ biri n’ime ọhịa na onwe ha.
translations.reference: Others are alleged to have been brought up by animals; some are said to have lived in the wild on their own.
translations.hypothesis: Others are accused of stealing or killing livestock; some are reportedly killed by wildlife defending themselves.

translations.source: Mgbe anumanu na-abughi-mmadu zulitechara ya kpam-kpam, nwa-ohia ahu egosi akparama-agwa (na njedebe ebe ana ahu anya) ihe dika nani nke anumanu-nlekota ya, dika ujo ya nye maobu enweghi ujo nye umu mmadu.
translations.reference: When completely brought up by non-human animals, the feral child exhibits behaviors (within physical limits) almost entirely like those of the particular care-animal, such as its fear of or indifference to humans.
translations.hypothesis: When the non-human primate was bitten, the virus was transmitted to the human through unprotected contact with the victim’s bodily fluids.

translations.source: Dịka ọmụmụ dabere n’arụmarụ kwesịrị ime ka ọmụmụ kara dị mfe ma na-adọkwu mmasị, ịkụ skafoldu gakwuru otu ụzọụkwụ n’ihu.
translations.reference: While project based learning should make learning easier and more interesting, scaffolding goes a step beyond.
translations.hypothesis: As an example, based on the destruction of the temple, the Passover lamb had to be killed earlier in the day than before.

translations.source: Skafoldin abụghị usoro mmụta kama ọ bụ enyemaka na-akwado ndị na-amụ ihe ọhụrụ dịka iji program ọhụrụ arụ ọrụ na kọmputa maọbụ ibido ọrụ ọhụrụ
translations.reference: Scaffolding is not a method of learning but rather an aid that provides support to individuals whom are undergoing a new learning experience such as using a new computer program or beginning a new project.
translations.hypothesis: A scaffold is not a teaching method in itself but a support structure for learners engaged in meaningful learning activities such as using a new software program or conducting a new project.

translations.source: Ụmụ arụrụmarụ osisi nwere ike ịbụ ma kendịnuche ma ịdịrị ire, n'ụzọ ọzọ, onye nkuzi bụ ụdị arụrụmarụ osisi mana ọ dịkwa dị ka nwoke ntakịrị mkpado akwụkwọ n'ime Microsoft Office.
translations.reference: Scaffolds can be both virtual and real, in other words, a teacher is a form of scaffold but so is the little paperclip man in Microsoft Office.
translations.hypothesis: A tree structure can be hierarchical or non-hierarchical, whereas an outline is a hierarchical tree structure but with a more rigid formatting similar to a bullet list in Microsoft Office.

translations.source: A rụnyechara Ihe nkwado n'ime ngwanro a, ndị ga-ajụ ajụjụ, nye ozi, ma kọwaa usoro ndị gaara ara nwa akwụkwọ ahụ ịghọta n'onwe ya.
translations.reference: Virtual Scaffolds are internalized in the software and are meant to question, prompt, and explain procedures that may have been to challenging for the student to handle alone.
translations.hypothesis: The support is built into the app, providing answers, information, and guiding the user through the process of self-discovery.

translations.source: Enwere ọtụtụ ihe e ji akpọga ụmụ aka ka onye ọzọ lekọta ha, dịka nleghara anya, mmegbu, nakwa nnapụ ihe.
translations.reference: Children are placed in Foster Care for a wide variety of reasons that range from neglect, to abuse, and even to extortion.
translations.hypothesis: There are many forms of physical abuse, such as hitting, slapping, pushing, and shaking.

translations.source: Ọ dị mma ka nwatakịrị tolite na gburugburu ebe a na-adịghị elekọta, elekọta, na agụmakwụkwọ, mana ha na-eme ya.
translations.reference: No child should ever have to grow up in an environment that is not nurturing, caring, and educational, but they do.
translations.hypothesis: It is best for a child to grow up in a stable, loving, and educated environment, but they don't.

translations.source: Anyị na-ahụta Ụkpụrụ Nlekọta anya ahụ ka ebe n’enweghi ihe iyi ndụ egwu nye ụmụaka ndị a.
translations.reference: We perceive the Foster Care System to be a safety zone for these children.
translations.hypothesis: We see the Compassionate Care Standard as a safe haven for these children.

translations.source: Ụlọ nchekwa ụmụaka anyị kwesịrị inye ụlọ nwere nchekwa, ndị nledo anya nwere ịhụnanya, nkụzi akwụkwọ dị mma, na nlekọta ahụike dị ntụkwasịobi.
translations.reference: Our foster care system is supposed to provide safe homes, loving caregivers, stable education, and reliable health care.
translations.hypothesis: Our day care facilities should provide a safe and stimulating environment, with caring and attentive supervision, enriching learning experiences, and reliable health care.

translations.source: Ulo nlekọta anya ndi akpotara-akpota kwesiri inyecha ihe nile di mkpa nke na adighi n’ulo ochie esi na kpota ha.
translations.reference: Foster care is supposed to provide all the necessities that were lacking in the home they were previously taken from.
translations.hypothesis: Detention facilities should provide the same standard of care as in the community.

translations.source: Ịntanetị na-ejikọ akụkụ nke nkwukọrịta ọha na nkwukọrịta nke mmadụ abụọ.
