translations.reference: Blogs can also help improve student writing. While students often begin their blog experience with sloppy grammar and spelling, the presence of an audience generally changes that.
translations.hypothesis: Blogs can also help students improve their writing. Since students often share their blog posts on social media, the presence of an audience encourages them to edit their work.

translations.source: Ebe ọ bụ na ụmụ akwụkwọ na-abụkarị ndị nkiri kachasị mkpa, odee blọọgụ ahụ na-amalite ịgbalị imelite odide ya iji zere nkatọ.
translations.reference: Since students are often the most critical audience, the blog writer begins to strive to improve writing to avoid criticism.
translations.hypothesis: Since academics are usually the harshest critics, the blogger begins trying to justify his post to avoid any negative comments.

translations.source: Nakwa ime blọọgụ "na-akwanye ụmụakwụkwọ ịmatakwu ihe gbasara ụwa gbara ha gburugburu." Mkpa nke ịkwalite mmasị nke ndị nkiri na-akpali ụmụakwụkwọ inwe amamihe ma na-adọrọ mmasị (Toto, 2004).
translations.reference: Also blogging "forces students to become more savvy about the world around them." The need to feed the interest of the audience inspires students to be clever and interesting (Toto, 2004).
translations.hypothesis: Also blogging "can help students make sense of the world around them." The need to develop students’ interest and curiosity is emphasised by several researchers (Totten, 2004).

translations.source: Ide blogu bu ngwa oru na akpalite mmekorita, o na akwadokwa umuakwukwo ka ha gbatiaa mmuta ha karia mmuta n’ulo akwukwo.
translations.reference: Blogging is a tool that inspires collaboration, and encourages students to extend learning well beyond the traditional school day.
translations.hypothesis: Blogging is a skill booster and helps learners to take their learning beyond the confines of the four walls of the classroom.

translations.source: Ojiji kwesịrị ekwesị nke ụmụ blọọgụ "nwere ike inye ụmụ akwụkwọ ike iji dịkwuo na kennyocha na ichekwu echiche; site n'ịza ọsịsọ n'ụmụ ihe ịntaneet, ụmụ akwụkwọ nwere ike ịkọwa ọnọdụ ha na nghọta nke ụmụ ederede ndị ọzọ ya na kwupụtachaa uche onwe ha n'ụmụ nsogbu pụrụ iche (Oravec, 2002).
translations.reference: Appropriate use of blogs "can empower students to become more analytical and critical; through actively responding to Internet materials, students can define their positions in the context of others' writings as well as outline their own perspectives on particular issues (Oravec, 2002).
translations.hypothesis: Meaningful use of blogs can provide students with a platform to further their thinking and engage in critical analysis; by responding to one another's posts on the blogs, students can clarify their positions and understanding of the material, as well as challenge one another's assumptions (Oravec, 2002).

translations.source: Ottawa bu isi obodo mara mma, nwere asusu abuo nke Canada ma nwekwa galari nka na ebe ngosi nka di iche iche n’egosiputa Canada n’oge gara aga ma n’oge ugbu a.
translations.reference: Ottawa is Canada's charming, bilingual capital and features an array of art galleries and museums that showcase Canada's past and present.
translations.hypothesis: Ottawa is a beautiful city, the capital of Canada and home to the National Gallery of Canada and several other museums and art galleries that explore Canada's past and present.

translations.source: Igakwuo ndida bu Mkpoda-mmiri Niagara ma mpaghara ugwu bu ulo nye nma udidi na emetubeghi aka nke Muskoka ma gafere.
translations.reference: Farther south is Niagara Falls and the north is home to the untapped natural beauty of the Muskoka and beyond.
translations.hypothesis: Further attractions include Niagara Falls and the Muskoka cottage country, a summer resort area.

translations.source: Ihe ndị a niile na ọzọ na-egosipụta Ọntario dị ka ihe echere na ọ bụ site n'ogo kachasị zuo oke Ndị Kanada site n'aka ndị ọbịa.
translations.reference: All these things and more highlight Ontario as what is considered quintessentially Canadian by outsiders.
translations.hypothesis: All these and more contribute to making Ontario the number one tourist destination in Canada.

translations.source: Ebe ndị buru ibu na ngapụga ugwu bụ ọzara nke obere ndị mmadụ bi ma ụfọdụ fọrọ nke nta ka ọ bụrụ ebe ndị mmadụ ebighị.
translations.reference: Large areas further north are quite sparsely populated and some is nearly uninhabited wilderness.
translations.hypothesis: The high plateaus and rugged mountains are sparsely populated and some areas are virtually uninhabitable.

translations.source: Otu ntule ọnụ ọgụgụ na-agbagwoju ọtụtụ ndị mmadụ anya: Ndị isi ojii amerịka bi na mba Amerịka karịrị ndị Kanada bi ebe ahụ n'ọnụ ọgụgụ.
translations.reference: For a comparison of population that surprises many: There are more African Americans living in the US than there are Canadian citizens.
translations.hypothesis: One surprising statistic: There are more black-owned businesses in the United States than there are Canadian-owned businesses.

translations.source: Obodo-akuku-mmiri nke ndi Owuwa-anyanwu Africa di na Osimiri India na opupu onu mmiri owuwa-anyanwu Africa.
translations.reference: The East African Islands are in the Indian Ocean off the eastern coast of Africa.
translations.hypothesis: The African plate is composed of the African continent and several surrounding tectonic plates including the Arabian plate and the Somali plate.

translations.source: Madagaaka kachasị buo ibu, ma bụrụkwa kọntinentị nọọrọ onwe ya ma a bịa n'ihe gbasara anụmanụ ndị bi n'ọhịa.
translations.reference: Madagascar is by far the biggest, and a continent on its own when it comes to wildlife.
translations.hypothesis: It is the largest and most diverse continent in terms of animals.

translations.source: Ọtụtụ agwaetiti ndị ka obere bụ mba ndị kwụụrụ onwe ha, maọbụ nọrọ na njiko ha na France, ndị a makwaara dịka rezọt ọnụ osimiri bu ebe mkporindụ.
translations.reference: Most of the smaller islands are independent nations, or associated with France, and known as luxury beach resorts.
translations.hypothesis: Many of the smaller islands are independent nations or are closely associated with France, and these so-called overseas departments are major tourist destinations.

translations.source: Ndị Arabụ wetekwara okpukpere Alakụba n'ala ndị ahụ, ma a nabatara ya nke ukwuu na mba Komoros na Mayọtụ.
translations.reference: The Arabs also brought Islam to the lands, and it took in a big way in the Comoros and Mayotte.
translations.hypothesis: Arabs also brought Islam to these lands, which is still widely spoken in Comoros and Mayotte.

translations.source: Ike onwunwe ndị Yurop ọchịchị ala ọzọ bidoro n’ime narị afọ nke iri na ise, dị ka one ngagharị one Pọtugalụ Vasco da Gama chọtara Ụzọ Kepụ site na Yurop ruo Indịa.
translations.reference: European influence and colonialism began in the 15th century, as Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama found the Cape Route from Europe to India.
translations.hypothesis: European powers began to colonize in the fifteenth century, when the Portuguese navigator Vasco da Gama found a sea route from Europe to India.

translations.source: N'akụkụ ugwu, Sahel gbara mpaghara a ogige; na ndịda ma n'ọdịda anyanwụ, Oke osimiri atlantik gbara ya ogige.
translations.reference: In the north the region is bounded by the Sahel, and in the south and west by the Atlantic Ocean.
translations.hypothesis: In the north, the Sahelian zone forms a transition belt towards the Sahara; in the south and southwest, the Atlantic Ocean forms its natural boundary.

translations.source: Ụmụ nwanyị: Ọ bụ ihe akwadoro na ndị njem nwanyị ọ bụla kwuo na ha alụọla dị, n'agbanyeghị etu ọnọdụ ha dị n'ezie.
translations.reference: Women: It is recommended that any women travellers say that they are married, regardless of actual marital status.
translations.hypothesis: Women: It is generally expected that any female traveller who is not obviously pregnant should state that she is not.

translations.source: Ọ na-enyekwara aka ịgba otu ọlaaka (naanị ọ bụghị nke yiri ka ọ dị oke ọnụ).
translations.reference: It is helpful to also wear a ring (just not one that looks too expensive.
translations.hypothesis: It also allows for more complex (and thus more interesting) animations.

translations.source: Ụmụ nwanyị kwesịrị ịghọta na ndịiche omenala nwere ike ịkpata ihe ha ga-ewere dị ka ịchọ okwu ma ọ bụghị ihe a na-ara ahụ ịhụ isoro gị, ijide site n'aka, dgz.
translations.reference: Women should realize that cultural differences may result in what they would consider harassment and it is not uncommon to be followed, grabbed by the arm, etc.
translations.hypothesis: Women should be aware that cultural differences may cause what they consider to be normal conversation or acceptable touching (e.g. hand holding, arm around the shoulder) to be considered flirtatious or even offensive.

translations.source: Guzosie ike n'ịsị ụmụ nwoke mba, ma atụla egwu ịkwechiri (na-agbanyeghi ọdịnala ọbụla nke ọ bụ, o kwesighi ekwesi!).
translations.reference: Be firm in turning down men, and don't be afraid to stand your ground (cultural differences or not, it doesn't make it ok!).
translations.hypothesis: Be wary of men who are too eager to please (regardless of their other qualities, this is a big red flag!).

translations.source: Obodo nke Casablanca nke ugbu a bụ Berber fishermen wubere ya na BCE narị afọ nke iri, ma ndị Phoenicia, Rome, na ndị Merenid jiri ya dị ka ọdụ ụgbọ mmiri dị oke mkpa akpọrọ Anfa.
translations.reference: The modern city of Casablanca was founded by Berber fishermen in the 10th century BCE, and was used by the Phoenicians, Romans, and the Merenids as a strategic port called Anfa.
translations.hypothesis: The present city of Casablanca was founded by Berbers in the 10th century BCE, and was used by the Phoenicians, Romans, and Merenids as an important port called Anfa.

translations.source: Ndị Pọtụgaalụ bibiri ya ma rụgharịa ya n’okpuru aha Casa Branca, naanị ịgbahapụ ya mgbe otu ala ọma jijiji mechara n’ime 1755.
translations.reference: The Portuguese destroyed it and rebuilt it under the name Casa Branca, only to abandon it after an earthquake in 1755.
translations.hypothesis: The Portuguese rebuilt and renamed it Casa Branca, only for it to be destroyed in the 1755 earthquake.

translations.source: Sọltan Ndị Moroko ahụ rụgharịrị obodo ahụ dị ka Darụ-I-Badya ma e nyere ya aha Casablanka site n'aka Ndị Spen na-azụ ahịa ndị wubere isi ebe ndị a na-ere ahịa ebe ahụ.
translations.reference: The Moroccan sultan rebuilt the city as Daru l-Badya and it was given the name Casablanca by Spanish traders who established trading bases there.
translations.hypothesis: The Moroccan sultan rebuilt the city and gave it the name Casablanca, from the Spanish words for "white house", referring to the whitewashed buildings in the area.

translations.source: Casablanca bụ otu n'ime opekata mpe ebe na-adọrọ mmasị ịzụ ahịa na Morocco niile.
translations.reference: Casablanca is one of the least interesting places to shop in all of Morocco.
translations.hypothesis: Casablanca is one of the most interesting shopping destinations in all of Morocco.

translations.source: Gburugburu Medina ochie ahụ ọ dị mfe ịchọta ebe ndị na-ere ụmụ ngwaahịa ọdịnala Ndị Moroko, dị ka ụmụ tagịnị, ite akpụrụ akpụ, ngwaahịa ejiri akpụkpọ anụ mee, huuka, na giigawụ nke ụdịdị dị iche iche zuru ezu, mana ha nille bụ maka ndị nleta.
translations.reference: Around the old Medina it's easy to find places selling traditional Moroccan goods, such as tagines, pottery, leather goods, hookahs, and a whole spectrum of geegaws, but it's all for the tourists.
translations.hypothesis: The old Medina is the best place to find traditional Moroccan products, such as babouches, pottery, leather goods, kaftans, and a wide variety of carpets, but the prices are often high for tourists.

translations.source: Goma bụ obodo nleta nke Democratic Replublic nke Kongo n'ime akụkụ ọwụwa anyanwụ kachasị anya na nso Rwanda.
translations.reference: Goma is a tourist city of the Democratic Republic of Congo in the extreme east near Rwanda.
translations.hypothesis: Goma is a city in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and a border town with Rwanda.

translations.source: N'afọ 2002, ebibiri Goma site n’aka lava si na ugwu ọkụ Nyiragongo nke liri ọtụtụ n'okporoama obodo, ọ kachasị etiti obodo.
translations.reference: In 2002 Goma was destroyed by lava from the Nyiragongo volcano which buried most of the town’s streets, particularly the town centre.
translations.hypothesis: In 2002, Goma was destroyed by lava from the nearby Nyiragongo volcano, which flowed down the streets and through the town centre.

translations.source: Dịka Goma nwetụrụ nchekwa n’ụdị dịtụ mma, nleta ọ bụla na mpụga Goma bụ nke ekwesịrị inyocha iji ghọta ọnọdụ nke ọgụ ka nogidesiri ike n’Ugwu ngalaba ọchịchị kizu.
translations.reference: While Goma is reasonably safe, any visits outside of Goma should be researched to understand the state of the fighting that persists in the North Kivu province.
translations.hypothesis: As Goma remains relatively secure, any excursion outside Goma should be undertaken with a good understanding of the security situation in the affected areas of North Kivu.

translations.source: Obodo ahụ bụkwa ntọala ịrị ugwu mgbawa Nyiragongo tinyere ụfọdụ nsochi Ọzọdimgba Ugwu dịchasị ọnụ ala n'Afrịka.
translations.reference: The city is also the base to climb the Nyiragongo volcano along with some of the cheapest Mountain Gorilla tracking in Africa.
translations.hypothesis: The city is also the base for climbing Nyiragongo, and some of the other volcanoes in the Virunga Massif, a mountain range in Central Africa.

translations.source: Ị nwere ike iji boda-boda (tagzi ọgba tum tum) ịga gburugburu Goma. Ọnụahịa nkịtị (ebeụlọ) bụ Francs Ndị Congo ~500 maka ọkwụkwọ dị mkpirikpi.
translations.reference: You can use boda-boda (motorcycle taxi) to get around Goma. The normal (local) price is ~500 Congolese Francs for the short ride.
translations.hypothesis: You can get around Goma using moto-taxis (sometimes called "bicycle taxis"). The normal fare (as of 2018) is around 500 Congolese Francs for a short ride.

translations.source: Tinyere na ira-ahu na nweta ya karia ibe ya, "Timbuktu" aburula ihe eji ama-atu maka ala ndi di anya, di oke-onu.
translations.reference: Combined with its relative inaccessibility, "Timbuktu" has come to be used as a metaphor for exotic, distant lands.
translations.hypothesis: In addition to the fame and the prestige, "Timbuktu" has brought a great deal of visibility to the desert country.

translations.source: Taa, Timbuktu obodo agụọ na-egbu, agbanyeghị n'ugwu ya na-eme ya otu ndọta ndị nleta, na o nwere otu ọdụ ụgbọelu.
translations.reference: Today, Timbuktu is an impoverished town, although its reputation makes it a tourist attraction, and it has an airport.
translations.hypothesis: Today, Timbuktu is a quiet town, though its airport does see some traffic, and it remains a tourist attraction.

translations.source: N'afọ 1990, e debanyere ya n'etiti ebe ọpụrụiche n'ụwa ndị nọ na nsogbu mkpochapụ, maka nsogbu aja si n'ọzara.
translations.reference: In 1990, it was added to the list of world heritage sites in danger, due to the threat of desert sands.
translations.hypothesis: In 1990, it was listed among the World's 100 most endangered sites, due to the effects of acid rain.

translations.source: Ọ bụ otu isi nkwụsịtụ n'oge Henry Louis Gates Ihe-ebube pụrụ iche PBS nke Ụwa Afrịka.
translations.reference: It was one of the major stops during Henry Louis Gates' PBS special Wonders of the African World.
translations.hypothesis: It was the subject of a recent Henry Louis Gates Jr. special on PBS called Faces of America.

translations.source: Obodo ahụ dị n'ọdịiche kachasị ya n'ụmụ obodo nke mba ahụ fọdụrụnụ, n'ihi na o nwere karịa mmasị nke Arabik karịa otu Onye Afrịka.
translations.reference: The city is in stark contrast to the rest of the country's cities, because it has more of an Arabic flair than of an African.
translations.hypothesis: The city is culturally more diverse than the rest of the country, and has a more liberal social attitude.

translations.source: Obianụọhịa Kemba Kruger (KNP) nọ n'ebe ugwu-ọwụwa anyanwu nke South Afrịka ma nọrọ ogologo ókè ahụ nke Mozambik n'ime ọwụwa anyanwụ, Zimbabwe n'ime ebe ugwu, na ókè ebe ndịda ahụ bụ Osimmiri Agụiyi.
translations.reference: The Kruger National Park (KNP) lies in the north-east of South Africa and runs along the border of Mozambique in the east, Zimbabwe in the north, and the southern border is the Crocodile River.
translations.hypothesis: Kruger National Park (KNP) is in the northeast of South Africa and is bordered by Mozambique in the east, Zimbabwe in the north and the Indian Ocean to the east.

translations.source: Ogige a ruru 19,500 km² nakwa ekewara ya n'ụzọ mpaghara ecozone 14, ebe nke ọbụla na-akwado ụdịrị anụ ọhịa dị iche.
translations.reference: The park covers 19,500 km² and is divided in 14 different ecozones, each supporting different wildlife.
translations.hypothesis: The park is 19,500 km2 in size and is divided into 14 different ecozones, each supporting a unique biodiversity.

translations.source: Ọ bụ otu n’ime nke isi ihe ndọta nke Ndịda Afrịka ma a na-ewe ya dị ka nke kacha mma nke Ebennọkọta Nkeobodo (SANParks) Ndịda Afrịka.
translations.reference: It is one of the main attractions of South Africa and it is considered the flagship of South African National Parks (SANParks).
translations.hypothesis: It is one of the main goals of South African tourism and is considered a flagship property of South African National Parks (SANParks).

translations.source: Dịka o si adị n'ogige mba niile nọ na Sawụtụ Afrịka, e nwere ụgwọ nchekwa n mbanye a na-akwụ kwa ụbọchị n'ogige a.
translations.reference: As with all South African National Parks, there are daily conservation and entry fees for the park.
translations.hypothesis: Like most countries in Southern Africa, there is a daily conservation fee charged at this park.

translations.source: O nwekwara ike iba uru ka mmadu gote Kaadi Ohia nke ga-enye gi ikikere iji banye na ogige ahoputagoro na South Africa ma o bu na Ogige Kemba South Africa niile.
translations.reference: It may also be beneficial for one to buy a Wild Card, which provides entry to either selections of parks in South Africa or all of the South African National Parks.
translations.hypothesis: It may also be advantageous to obtain a Wild Card, which allows you entry to all caves in the Southern Cape, and is cheaper than paying for each cave individually.

translations.source: Ọ bụ site na Agwaetiti Họng Kọng ka mpaghara Họng Kọng nwetara aha ya; Ọ bụkwa ebe a ka ndị njem nlereanya na-ahụta dịka ebe kachasị mkpa.
translations.reference: Hong Kong Island gives the territory of Hong Kong its name and is the place that many tourists regard as the main focus.
translations.hypothesis: It is from Hong Kong Island that the region gets its name; it is also where most of the tourist attractions are located.

translations.source: E jirila ụmụ ogologo ụlọ elu na-achọ igwe Họng Kọng mma maa atụ na ha yiri eserese baa chat, nke mmiri Viktoria Habọ mere ka ọ pụta ihe.
translations.reference: The parade of buildings that make the Hong Kong skyline has been likened to a glittering bar chart that is made apparent by the presence of the waters of Victoria Harbour.
translations.hypothesis: The skyscrapers of Hong Kong are often compared to a beautiful piece of abstract art, and Victoria Harbour is the perfect place to take in the view.

translations.source: Ịhụta Họng Kọng n'ụzọ kachasị mma, pụọ n'agwaetiti gawa na Kowloon, mpaghara akụkụ mmiri, nke chere gị ihu.
translations.reference: To get the best views of Hong Kong, leave the island and head for the Kowloon waterfront opposite.
translations.hypothesis: To get the best view of the Hong Kong skyline, head to Kowloon, the area across Victoria Harbour from Hong Kong Island, and look across the water.

translations.source: Oke ihe ka n'ọnụ ọgụgụ n'ime mmepe obodo nke Agwaetiti Hong Kong jupụtara n'ọnụ na ala a napụtara na mmiri dị n'ogologo ụzọ nke ugwu akụkụ oke osimiri.
translations.reference: The great majority of Hong Kong Island's urban development is densely packed on reclaimed land along the northern shore.
translations.hypothesis: Much of Hong Kong's urban area occupies a relatively small area of land at the end of a long, narrow peninsula.

translations.source: Ebe a bụ ebe ndị nchịkwa mba si Britenụ were dịka nke ha ya mere ọ bụrụ na ị na-achọ maka akaebe nke nchịkwa ókèala ahụ gara aga, ebe a bụ ebe dị mma ịmalite.
translations.reference: This is the place the British colonisers took as their own and so if you are looking for evidence of the territory's colonial past, this is a good place to start.
translations.hypothesis: Here is where the British established their first colony so if you are looking for a starting point for British colonial history this is it.

translations.source: Ebe Sundarbans bụ ebe ala nwere ọhịa mmiri nọ n'akụkụ mmiri kachasị ukwuu n'ụwa dum, na-agbatị ruo kilomita 80 (50 mi) n'ime n'ala Bangladesh na India ahụ nke amaghị ama site n'ụsọ osimiri.
translations.reference: The Sundarbans are the largest littoral mangrove belt in the world, stretching 80 km (50 mi) into the Bangladeshi and Indian hinterland from the coast.
translations.hypothesis: The Sundarbans is the largest mangrove forest in the world, sprawling across 80 km (50 mi) into the Indian Ocean delta in Bangladesh and India.

translations.source: E kwupụtawo na Sundarbans bụ otu Ebe Nketa Keụwa UNESCO. Akụkụ nke oke ọhịa n'ime ókèala nke Indịa ka a na-akpọ Obianụọhịa Kemba Sundarbans.
translations.reference: The Sundarbans has been declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The part of the forest within Indian territory is called Sundarbans National Park.
translations.hypothesis: The Sundarbans is also designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Indian part of the forest is known as the Sundarbans National Park.

translations.source: Ọhịa ndị a abụghịkwa sọọsọ apịtị mangrov dị na ha – ha gụnyekwara ihe ndị ka fọrọ site n'oke ọhịa ndị juburu Ala nọ na mpaghara Ganjiz.
translations.reference: The forests aren't just mangrove swamps though — they include some of the last remaining stands of the mighty jungles which once covered the Gangetic plain.
translations.hypothesis: These forests are not just composed of mangrove trees – they also include other plant life such as coconut palms and fruit trees that grow inland along the Ganjiz region.

translations.source: Sundabans kpuchiri ohere km² 3850, nke mmiri maọbụ ala apịtị kpuchiri otu ụzọ n'ụzọ atọ ya.
translations.reference: The Sundarbans cover an area of 3,850 km², of which about one-third is covered in water/marsh areas.
translations.hypothesis: The Sundarbans cover 3850 square kilometres (1486 sq mi) of which one-third is land and the rest is water.

translations.source: Ka mgbe 1966, ka Sundarbans ji buru ebe obibi nso anu ohia ana asi na aga enwe ihe dika 400 Royal Bengal tiger na ihe dika 30,000 mgbada nwere ntupo na mpaghara ebe ahu.
translations.reference: Since 1966 the Sundarbans have been a wildlife sanctuary, and it is estimated that there are now 400 Royal Bengal tigers and about 30,000 spotted deer in the area.
translations.hypothesis: As of 1966, the Sundarbans supported an estimated 400 Royal Bengal tigers and 30,000 spotted deer.

translations.source: Bọọsụ na-esi n'ọdụ ụgbọala njikọ-mpaghara apụ (n'ofe osimiri ahụ) mgbe niile n'ụbọchị, agbanyeghị na nke kacha, tụmadị ndị ahụ na-aga n'ebe ọwụwaanyanwụ na Jakar/Bumthang na-apụ n'etiti 06:30 na 07:30.
translations.reference: Buses depart the inter-district bus station (across the river) throughout the day, though most, especially those heading to the east and Jakar/Bumthang leave between 06:30 and 07:30.
translations.hypothesis: Buses from the central bus station (across the river) depart several times daily, although most, especially those heading to the eastern districts of Jakar/Bumthang, leave between 06:30 and 07:30.

translations.source: Dị ka ụmụ bọọsụ njikọ-mpaghara na-ejukarị eju, ọ bụ ezi ndụmọdụ ịzụta otu tiketi ụbọchị ole na ole n'ọdịnihu.
translations.reference: As the inter-district buses are often full, it is advisable to purchase a ticket a few days in advance.
translations.hypothesis: As regional buses are usually fully booked, it is a good idea to buy a ticket a day in advance.

translations.source: A na-ejere imirikiti mpaghara ozi site n'ụmụ Nnukwu Bọọsụ nke ndị Japan, nke dị mma ma sie ike.
translations.reference: Most districts are served by small Japanese Coaster Buses, which are comfortable and sturdy.
translations.hypothesis: Most areas are served by Japan's excellent and efficient bus network.

translations.source: Tagzi ekere eke bụ ụzọ dị ọsịsọ ma maa mma iji gaa ebe dị nso, dịka Paro (Nu 150) na Punakha (Nu 200).
translations.reference: Shared taxis are a quick and comfortable means to travel to nearby places, such as Paro (Nu 150) and Punakha (Nu 200).
translations.hypothesis: Taxis are a fast and convenient way to get around, but more expensive, than buses, for example Paro to Thimphu (Nu 150) or Paro to Punakha (Nu 200).

translations.source: Akwammiri Osimiri Oyapock bụ otu akwa mmiri ejiri kebùl runye ya. Ọ gbara gburugburu Osimiri Oyapock iji jikọọ ụmụ obodo nke Oiapoque n'ime Brazịl na Saint-Georges de l'Oyapock n'ime French Guiana.
translations.reference: The Oyapock River Bridge is a cable-stayed bridge. It spans the Oyapock River to link the cities of Oiapoque in Brazil and Saint-Georges de l'Oyapock in French Guiana.
translations.hypothesis: The Oyapock River is a natural border between French Guiana and Brazil. It is crossed by the Friendship Bridge, a cable-stayed bridge, which connects the towns of Oiapoque in Brazil and Saint-Georges-de-l'Oyapock in French Guiana.

translations.source: Towa abuo ahu rigoro 83 meters, ogologo o bu 378 meters n’ogologo ma o nwekwara obodobo uzo abuo di 3.50m.
translations.reference: The two towers rise to a height of 83 meters, it's 378 meters long and it has two lanes of 3.50 m wide.
translations.hypothesis: The two towers are 83 metres (272 ft) tall, 378 metres (1,240 ft) long and 3.50 metres (11.5 ft) wide.

translations.source: Ogologo ahụ ya kwụ-ọtọ nke akwa mmiri ahụ bụ mita 15. A rụchara ọrụrụ ya n'Ọgọọst 2011, e mepeghị ya nye ụgbọala ruo Maachị 2017.
translations.reference: The vertical clearance under the bridge is 15 meters. Construction was completed in August 2011, it didn't open to traffic until March 2017.
translations.hypothesis: The tunnel's length is 15 metres. It was completed in August 2011, but not opened to traffic until March 2017.

translations.source: E hiwere na akwa ahụ ga-ebido rụwa ọrụ n'uju na Septemba 2017, mgbe a na-ele anya ịrụcha ebe nnyocha nke ụlọọrụ na-ahụ maka ọpụpụ na mbata nke ndị Brazili.
translations.reference: The bridge is scheduled to be fully operational in September 2017, when the Brazilian customs checkpoints are expected to be finished.
translations.hypothesis: The tunnel was due to open in September 2017, after a survey of the Brazilian side of the border was completed.

translations.source: Ndị Guaraní bụ otu amaala kachasị gbaa ọkpụrụkpụrụ bi n'eba a na-akpọ ugbua Ọwụwaanyanwụ Paragụwa, ha na-ebi ka ndị dinta na-awagharị awagharị ma na-arụkwa ọrụ ugbo mmepụta nri nke onwe.
translations.reference: The Guaraní were the most significant indigenous group inhabiting what is now Eastern Paraguay, living as semi-nomadic hunters who also practised subsistence agriculture.
translations.hypothesis: The Guarani are an indigenous people who live in the subtropical region of Paraguay, living as hunter-gatherers and practicing agriculture.

translations.source: Mpaghara Chako bụ ụlọ nye ụfọdụ agbụrụ amaala ndị ọzọ dịka Guaykuru na Payagua, ndị ji nta, ntụtụkọ, na ịkụ azụ wee zụọ onwe ha nri.
translations.reference: The Chaco region was home to other groups of indigenous tribes such as the Guaycurú and Payaguá, who survived by hunting, gathering and fishing.
translations.hypothesis: The Chaco region is home to several other indigenous groups, such as the Guaykuru and Payaguá, who have traditionally lived off the land by hunting, gathering, and fishing.

translations.source: N'ime narị afọ nke iri na isii Paragwei, a kpọbụrụ "Nnukwu Ngalaba Ọchịchị nke Ndị Indii", bụ nke a mụrụ n'ihi mbịakwute nke ndị mmeri Ndị Spen ya na ụmụ òtù nwaafọ amaala.
translations.reference: In the 16th century Paraguay, formerly called "The Giant Province of the Indies", was born as a result of the encounter of Spanish conquerors with the native indigenous groups.
translations.hypothesis: In the 16th century Paraguay was known as the "Viceroyalty of the Indies", born from the Spanish conquerors' and natives' union.

translations.source: Ndị Spen bidoro oge ọchịchị ike nke digidere ruo narị afọ atọ.
translations.reference: The Spaniards started the colonization period which lasted for three centuries.
translations.hypothesis: The Spanish began a three-hundred-year domination.

translations.source: Kemgbe ntọala Asunción n’ime 1537, Paraguay agbalịala idobe ọtụtụ n’ime omume na njirimara amaala ya.
translations.reference: Since the foundation of Asunción in 1537, Paraguay has managed to keep a lot of its indigenous character and identity.
translations.hypothesis: Since the foundation of Asunción in 1537, Paraguay has tried to preserve many of its traditions and cultural identity.

translations.source: Amaara mba Ajentịna dịka obodo nwere ndị egwuregwu na otu egwuregwu polo kachasị mma n'ụwa dum.
translations.reference: Argentina is well known for having one of the best polo teams and players in the world.
translations.hypothesis: Argentina is known as the country of the best polo players in the world.

translations.source: Ndọrọndọrọ kachasị ukwu nke afọ ahụ na-eme na Disemba na fịịldị polo n’ime Las Cañitas.
translations.reference: The largest tournament of the year takes place in December at the polo fields in Las Cañitas.
translations.hypothesis: The biggest event of the year takes place in December at the Polos Field in Las Cañitas.

translations.source: Obere asọmpi ga na egwuregwu bọlụ ga ka e nwere ike ịhụ ebe a n'oge ụfọdụ n'afọ.
translations.reference: Smaller tournaments and matches can also be seen here at other times of the year.
translations.hypothesis: There will be less competition for spots on the team, and more time to get to know the other players.

translations.source: Maka akụkọ gbasara ụmụ ndorondoro na ebe a na-azụ tiketi maka egwuregwu polo, lelee Asociacion Argentina de Polo.
translations.reference: For news on tournaments and where to buy tickets for polo matches, check Asociacion Argentina de Polo.
translations.hypothesis: For information on schedules and where to buy polo tickets, see the Asociacion Argentina de Polo.

translations.source: Ego azụmahịa mba Fọlkụlandị bụ pam Fọlkụlandị (FKP) nke ọnụ ya na otu pam ndị Britenị (GBP) ha.
translations.reference: The official Falklands currency is the Falkland pound (FKP) whose value is set equivalent to that of one British pound (GBP).
translations.hypothesis: The currency of the Falkland Islands is the Falkland Pound (FKP), which is equal in value to the British Pound (GBP).

translations.source: E nere ike ime mgbanwe ego na naanị otu ụlọ akụ nọ n’agwaetiti ndị ahụ nke a ga-achọtali n’ime Stanley n’ofe site n’ụlọ ahịa FIC West.
translations.reference: Money can be exchanged at the only bank in the islands which is located in Stanley across from the FIC West store.
translations.hypothesis: The only currency exchange on the islands is located in Stanley and is run by the Falkland Islands Company (FIC) through its West Store.

translations.source: A ga-anabata n’izugbe pam ndị Britenụ ebe ọbụla n’ime agwaetiti ndị ahụ ma na gburugburu ụmụ kaadị mbiri ego Stanley na dọla mba Amerịka sokwa na ndị a na-anabata.
translations.reference: British pounds will generally be accepted anywhere in the islands and within Stanley credit cards and United States dollars are also often accepted.
translations.hypothesis: They are accepted throughout the UK and on most of the Channel Islands and are also widely accepted in the US and Canada.

translations.source: N’agwaetiti ndị nọ na mpụga ebe ahụ ụmụ kaadị akwụmụgwọ nwere ike a gaghị anabata ya, n’agbanyeghị na enwere ike iwe ego Britenụ na United States; leru anya na ndị nwe ya n’ọdịnihu iji chọpụta ihe bụ ụzọ nkwụmụgwọ a na-anabata.
translations.reference: On the outlying islands credit cards will probably not be accepted, although British and United States currency may be taken; check with the owners in advance to determine what is an acceptable payment method.
translations.hypothesis: Outside the main tourist areas, credit cards are unlikely to be accepted, though British and US dollars are widely accepted; check with your hotel or guesthouse to find out what the best options are.

translations.source: Ọ na-ara ezigbote ahụ ịgbanwe ego Falklands ma e si n'agwaetiti a pụọ, ya mere gbanwee ego gi tupu i si na ya pụọ.
translations.reference: It is nearly impossible to exchange Falklands currency outside of the islands, so exchange money prior to leaving the islands.
translations.hypothesis: It is cheaper to exchange money in the Falklands than to take it out of the islands, so exchange your money before you leave.

translations.source: Ebe Montevideo dị na ndịda Iquetọ, ọ bụ oge ọkọchị ebe ahụ mgbe oge oyi dị na Ebe ugwu Emisfee ma n'otu aka ahụ.
translations.reference: Since Montevideo is south of the Equator, it is summer there when it's winter in the Northern Hemisphere and vice versa.
translations.hypothesis: Located in the Southern Hemisphere, it is summer in Montevideo when it is winter in the Northern Hemisphere and vice versa.

translations.source: Montevideo nọ n'ime ebe na-ekpọ ọkụ ma jụọkwa oyi; n'ime ụmụ ọnwa ọkọchị, okpomọkụ gafere +30°C bụ ihe nkịtị.
translations.reference: Montevideo is in the subtropics; in the summer months, temperatures above +30°C are common.
translations.hypothesis: Montevideo has a subtropical climate with hot summers and mild winters; in the summer months, temperatures above +30 °C are not unusual.

translations.source: Oge oyi nwere ike ịjụ ezigbo oyi n'aghụghọ: okpomọkụ na-ara ahụ tupu ya gaa n'okpuru ịghọ okwute mmiri, mana ikuku na oruru mmiri na-abịakọta ọnụ ime ka o nwee mmetụta kara jụọ oyi karịa ihe temometa kwuru.
translations.reference: The winter can be deceptively chilly: temperatures rarely go below freezing, but the wind and humidity combine to make it feel colder than what the thermometer says.
translations.hypothesis: Cold weather can be deceptive: the air temperature can be well below freezing, but if the humidity is high, the air and water will feel much colder than the thermometer indicates.

translations.source: Enweghị ihe dị ka "udu mmiri" na "ọkọchị": ogo mmiri ozuzo na-anọkarị otu ebe ogologo afọ niile.
translations.reference: There are no particular "rainy" and "dry" seasons: the amount of rain stays roughly the same throughout the year.
translations.hypothesis: There is no such thing as "rainy season" and "dry season": the precipitation usually remains more or less constant throughout the year.

translations.source: Agbanyeghị na ọ maala ahụ ọtụtụ n'ime ụmụ anụmanụ nọ n'obianụmanụ ịhụ ndị mmadụ, ka o sina dị anụ ọhịa bụ nke azụghịazụ ma e kwesịghị inye ha nri ma ọ bụ nye ha nsogbu.
translations.reference: Though many of the animals in the park are used to seeing humans, the wildlife is nonetheless wild and should not be fed or disturbed.
translations.hypothesis: Although most animals are used to seeing humans, they should not be fed or approached closely.

translations.source: Site n'aka ndị na-ahụ maka ogige anụmanụ, nọtee aka opekata mpe yadị maọbụ mita 100 n'ebe anụ ọhịa bea na wulfu nọ na yadị maọbụ mita 25 n'ebe anụ ọhịa ndị ọzọ niile nọ!
translations.reference: According to park authorities, stay at least 100 yards/meters away from bears and wolves and 25 yards/meters from all other wild animals!
translations.hypothesis: From the park authorities, keep at least 100 yards (91 metres) away from bears and wolves and 25 yards (23 metres) away from all other wildlife!

translations.source: Agbanyeghị etu ha siri dị nwayọọ, bison, elk, muuz, bea, na anụmanụ ukwu niile nwere ike iluso ọgụ.
translations.reference: No matter how docile they may look, bison, elk, moose, bears, and nearly all large animals can attack.
translations.hypothesis: Despite their size, bison, elk, moose, bears, and other large mammals can be aggressive.

translations.source: Afọ ọ bụla, a na-emerụ ọtụtụ ndị nleta ahụ n'ihi na ha enyeghị ezigbo ohere. Ụmụ anụmanụ ndị a buru ibu, azụghịazụ, ma nweekkwa ike ịbụ ihe ize ndụ, ya mere nye ha ohere.
translations.reference: Each year, dozens of visitors are injured because they didn't keep a proper distance. These animals are large, wild, and potentially dangerous, so give them their space.
translations.hypothesis: Every year, several visitors are injured because they did not keep a safe distance. These are wild, unpredictable animals and can be dangerous, so keep your distance.

translations.source: Na mgbakwunye, mara amara na usi na adọta ụmụ bea na anụ ọhịa ndị ọzọ, ya mere zere ibu ma ọ bụ isi ụmụ nri na-esi usi ma debe kampụ dị ọcha.
translations.reference: In addition, be aware that odors attract bears and other wildlife, so avoid carrying or cooking odorous foods and keep a clean camp.
translations.hypothesis: Additionally, be aware that ticks can also transmit Lyme disease and other infections, so check yourself and your pets for ticks after being outdoors and keep your pet’s fur short.

translations.source: Apia bụ isi obodo Samoa. Obodo ahụ nọ n'agwaetiti Upolu ma ma nwee ngụpụta mmadụ nke ji obere ihe ghara eru 40,000.
translations.reference: Apia is the capital of Samoa. The town is on the island of Upolu and has a population of just under 40,000.
translations.hypothesis: Apia is the capital city of Samoa. The town is on the island of Upolu and has a population of just under 40,000 people.

translations.source: E kepụtara Apịa n'afọ ndị 1850; kemgbe 1959, ọ bụ isi obodo Samoa.
translations.reference: Apia was founded in the 1850s and has been the official capital of Samoa since 1959.
translations.hypothesis: Apia was founded in the 1850s; since 1959 it has been the capital of Samoa.

translations.source: Ọdụ ụgbọ mmiri ahụ bụ ebe nguzosike nke ndị agha mmiri wuru ewu na 1889 mgbe nnukwu ụgbọ mmiri asaa si Jamani, US, na Briten jụrụ ịhapụ ọdụ ụgbọ mmiri ahụ.
translations.reference: The harbor was the site of an infamous naval standoff in 1889 when seven ships from Germany, the US, and Britain refused to leave the harbor.
translations.hypothesis: The port is a military base established in 1889 when seven battleships from Germany, the US, and Britain refused to leave the port.

translations.source: Nnukwu ụgbọ mmiri niile ndị ahụ miri, ewezụga otu ụgbọ agha Ndị Briten. Ọ fọrọ obere ka o ruo Ndị Amerịka na Ndị Jamani 200 nwụrụnụ.
translations.reference: All the ships were sunk, except for one British cruiser. Nearly 200 American and German lives were lost.
translations.hypothesis: All of those ships were sunk, except for one British battleship. It cost the Americans and Germans about 200 lives.

translations.source: N'oge mgba maka nnwereonwe nke a haziri site n'aka ngagharị Mau, otu nzukọ keudo n'ime obodo rụpụtara n'ogbugbu nke ezigbo onyeisi Tupua Tamasese Lealofi III.
translations.reference: During the struggle for independence organised by the Mau movement, a peaceful gathering in the town resulted in the killing of the paramount chief Tupua Tamasese Lealofi III.
translations.hypothesis: In the ensuing melee for independence orchestrated by Mau, a coalition government was formed with the cooperation of Head Chief Tupua Tamasese Lealofi III.

translations.source: E nwere ọtụtụ ọnụ mmiri, n’ihi nnọnetiti nke Ọklandị nke ọdụ ụgbọ mmiri abụọ. Ndị nke kacha ewu ewu nọ n’ebe atọ.
translations.reference: There are many beaches, due to Auckland's straddling of two harbours. The most popular ones are in three areas.
translations.hypothesis: There are several marinas, due to the large number of yachts based in Auckland. The most popular has three.

translations.source: Akụkụ mmiri Ọnụmmiri Ugwu (nọ na mpaghara Ugwu Ebe ndote ụgbọ mmiri) nọ n’oke osimiri Pacifik ma dọtịa site na Long Bay nọ n’ugwu ruo Devonport nọ na ndịda.
translations.reference: North Shore beaches (in North Harbour district) are on the Pacific Ocean and stretch from Long Bay in the north to Devonport in the south.
translations.hypothesis: The North Shore (located on the North Island) is in the upper harbour and stretches from Long Bay in the north to Devonport in the south.

translations.source: Ha niile fọrọ obere ka ha bụrụchaa akụkụ mmiri aja aja ya na igwu mmiri echedoro echedo, ma ọtụtụ n'ime ha nwere ndo enyere site n'aka ụmụ osisi pohutukawa.
translations.reference: They are almost all sandy beaches with safe swimming, and most have shade provided by pohutukawa trees.
translations.hypothesis: They are all at least partially surrounded by a rocky beach and some of them are backed by a steep fringe of pohutukawa trees.

translations.source: Ụmụ akụkụ mmiri Tamaki Drive nọ n’Ọdụ ụgbọ mmiri Waitemata ahụ, n’ime ahịa ndị bara ụba nọ mpaghara ebe obibi nke Mission Bay na St Heliers n’ime Central Auckland.
translations.reference: Tamaki Drive beaches are on the Waitemata Harbour, in the upmarket suburbs of Mission Bay and St Heliers in Central Auckland.
translations.hypothesis: The Tamaki Drive waterfront is located in the Waitemata Harbour, within the affluent suburbs of Mission Bay and St Heliers in Eastern Auckland.

translations.source: Ebe ndị a bụ mgbe ụfọdụ akụkụ mmiri ezinụlọ ndị mmadụ juru ya n’ọtụtụ ụdị ụlọ ahịa nọ n’ogologo ọnụ mmiri ahụ. Igwu mmiri dị mma.
translations.reference: These are sometimes-crowded family beaches with a good range of shops lining the shore. Swimming is safe.
translations.hypothesis: These areas are sometimes family-run affairs with several shops along a long stretch of beach. The diving is good.

translations.source: Isi biya imeobodo ahụ bụ 'Number One', ọ bụghị biya na-agbagwoju anya, mana dị mma n'ahụ ma na-edo ahụ nke ọma. Biya imeobodo nke ọzọ bụ nke a na-akpọ "Manta".
translations.reference: The main local beer is 'Number One', it is not a complex beer, but pleasant and refreshing. The other local beer is called "Manta".
translations.hypothesis: The main attraction of the city is the "Number One" beach, which is not a very long beach, but a very nice and well-kept one. The second beach is called "Manta".

translations.source: Enwere ọtụtụ mmanya si Frans mmadụ ga-aṅụ, mana mmanya Niu Ziland na Ọstrelia ga-aka mma maka njem.
translations.reference: There are many French wines to be had, but the New Zealand and Australian wines might travel better.
translations.hypothesis: There are many fine French wines, but the wines of New Zealand and Australia are more suitable for a journey.

translations.source: Mmiri mgbata ebeụlọ dị mma nke ọma ịn̄ụ, mana mmiri bọtụlụ dị mfe ịchọta ma ọ bụrụ na ụjọ na-atụ gị.
translations.reference: The local tap water is perfectly safe to drink, but bottled water is easy to find if you are fearful.
translations.hypothesis: Tap water is generally safe to drink, but bottled water is readily available if you are concerned.

translations.source: Maka ndị Australia, kọfị 'flat white' bụ ihe ala ọzọ. Shọt blak bụ 'espresso', cappuccino na-ebu nnukwu krim abịa (ọ bụghị froth), ha na-añụ tii na-etinyeghị mmiri ara ehi.
translations.reference: For Australians, the idea of 'flat white' coffee is foreign. A short black is 'espresso', cappuccino comes heaped high with cream (not froth), and tea is served without milk.
translations.hypothesis: For Australians, a flat white is just another coffee. A short black is an espresso, a cappuccino is espresso with a large amount of foamed milk (not froth), and a long black is espresso with a dash of hot water.

translations.source: Chokoleeti ọkụ a ruru ogo nke Beljiọm. Mmanya mkpụrụ osisi dị ọnụ mana ha amaka.
translations.reference: The hot chocolate is up to Belgian standards. Fruit juices are pricey but excellent.
translations.hypothesis: This hot chocolate is a Belgian standard. The fruit brandies are reasonably priced and taste good.

translations.source: A na-eme ọtụtụ njem ịga na ime ala osimiri gburugburu afọ niile, ma mmerụ ahụ n'ihi otu n'ime ihe mkpata ndị a n'ime ala osimiri ahụ na-ara ahụ inweta.
translations.reference: Many trips to the reef are made all year around, and injuries due to any of these causes on the reef are rare.
translations.hypothesis: Many trips are made to the bottom of the ocean each year, and injuries from one of these causes is not uncommon.

translations.source: N’agbanyeghị, were ndụmọdụ si n'aka ndị nọ n’ọchịchị, rube isi n’ihe ntụaka niile, ma gee ntị nke ọma maka ịdọ aka na ntị nke nchekwa.
translations.reference: Still, take advice from authorities, obey all signs, and pay close attention to safety warnings.
translations.hypothesis: However, follow official advice, heed all warnings, and be extra careful about safety.

translations.source: Azụjelii igbe na-apụta n'akụkụ ọnụ osimiri ma n'ụso ụmụ njekọta osimiri site n'Ọktoba ruo Eprel ugwu nke 1770. E nwekwara ike ịhụ ha mgbe ụfọdụ n'oge ndị ọzọ n'abụghị oge ndị a.
translations.reference: Box jellyfish occur near beaches and near river estuaries from October to April north of 1770. They can occasionally be found outside these times.
translations.hypothesis: The whales are seen in the bay and along the coast from October to April. They can sometimes be seen at other times of the year.

translations.source: Shaakị gasị dị adị, otú ọ dị, ha adịkarịghị awakpo ụmụ mmadụ. Imirikiti shaakị na-atụ ụmụ mmadụ egwu yana ga-egwu mmiri pụọ.
translations.reference: Sharks do exist, however they rarely attack humans. Most sharks are scared of humans and would swim away.
translations.hypothesis: Sharks are often overfished, however, and rarely pose a threat to humans. Most sharks are wary of humans and will swim away.

translations.source: Agụiyi mmiri nnu anaghị ebikewe n'ime oke osimiri, ebe ha na-ebikarị bụ na ngwọkọta osimiri na mmiri nnu dị n'ugwu sitere na Rọkhamptịn.
translations.reference: Saltwater Crocodiles do not actively live in the ocean, their primary habitat is in river estuaries north from Rockhampton.
translations.hypothesis: The jellyfish do not normally swim in the open ocean, but are usually found in the intertidal zone and shallow waters around the rocky coasts of the North Sea.

translations.source: Itinye akwụkwọ n’ọdịnihu na-enye onye njem ahụ obi udo na ha nwere ebe ha ga-arahụ ụra ozugbo ha rutere ebe ha na-aga.
translations.reference: Booking in advance gives the traveller peace of mind that they will have somewhere to sleep once they arrive at their destination.
translations.hypothesis: Booking ahead gives the traveller the peace of mind of knowing they have a bed for the night when they arrive at their destination.

translations.source: Ndị nnọchi anya ndị njem na-enwekarị nkwekọ azụmahịa ha na kpọmkwem ụmụ họteelụ, agbanyeghị na ị nwere ike ịhụ na o kwere omume itinye akwụkwọ maka ụdị nnabata ndị ọzọ, dị ka ala ebe a na-ama ụlọikwu, sitere n'otu onye nnọchite anya njem.
translations.reference: Travel agents often have deals with specific hotels, although you may find it possible to book other forms of accommodation, like camping grounds, through a travel agent.
translations.hypothesis: Travel agents often have business relationships with particular hotels, though you may be able to book other types of accommodation, such as a bed in a hostel, through a travel agent.

translations.source: Ndị nnọchi anya ndị njem na-enyekarị ụmụ ngwungwu na-agụnye nri ụtụtụ, nhazi ụzọ esi eje njem ịga na/site na ọdụ ụgbọelu ma ọ bụ njem ụgbọelu etikọrọ ọnụ ya na ụmụ ngwungwu họteelụ.
translations.reference: Travel agents usually offer packages that include breakfast, transportation arrangements to/from the airport or even combined flight and hotel packages.
translations.hypothesis: Travel agents often provide packages that include hotel rooms, airport transfers and/or discounted airfare in addition to the packages offered by tour operators.

translations.source: Ha nwekwara ike idobere gị ohere a ma ọ bụrụ na ị ka chọrọ oge ịtụgharị uche na ya maọbụ ịnweta akwụkwọ ndị ọzọ maka ebe ị na-aga (ọmụmaatụ: visa).
translations.reference: They can also hold the reservation for you if you need time to think about the offer or procure other documents for your destination (e.g. visa).
translations.hypothesis: They may also give you more time to think about it or to obtain other documents such as passports.

translations.source: Ihe ọbụla a chọrọ ịgbanwe maọbụ ịna, ọ bụ onye ejenti njem ka a ga-ebu ụzọ gakwuru; ọ bụghị họteelụ n'onwe ya.
translations.reference: Any amendments or requests though should be coursed through the travel agent first and not directly with the hotel.
translations.hypothesis: Any changes or cancellations must go through the agent, not the hotel itself.

translations.source: Maka ụfọdụ mmemme, nnukwu ọtụtụ n’ime ndị bịara na mmemme egwu ahụ kpebiri ịnọ na kampụ n’ebe ahụ, ma ọtụtụ n’ime ndị bịara na-ewe ya otu akụkụ dị oke mkpa nke ahụmihe ahụ.
translations.reference: For some festivals, the vast majority of the attendants to music festivals decide to camp on site, and most attendants consider it a vital part of the experience.
translations.hypothesis: For some attendees, the best part of the music festival was the camping experience, and for many attendees, it was a core part of the experience.

translations.source: Ọ bụrụ na ị chọrọ ịnọ nso na emereme ahụ ị ga-ekwesị ịbanye ọsịịsọ iji nweta otu ebe a na-ama ụlọikwu nọ nso n'egwu ahụ.
translations.reference: If you want to be close to the action you're going to have to get in early to get a camping site close to the music.
translations.hypothesis: If you want to be close to the action you should book a hotel in the Theater District.

translations.source: Cheta na obu ezie na egwu ogbo-egwu nwere ike gwula, enwere ike inwe mpaghara mmeme ahu gana aku egwu ruo ime abali.
translations.reference: Remember that even though music on the main stages may have finished, there may be sections of the festival that will keep playing music until late into the night.
translations.hypothesis: Please note that although the music is usually turned down, there may be music at the pool area until late at night.

translations.source: Ụfọdụ ememme nwere ebe ndị a na-ama ụlọikwuu pụrụ iche maka ezinụlọ nke nwere ụmụ na-eto eto.
translations.reference: Some festivals have special camping areas for families with young children.
translations.hypothesis: Some events have areas specifically for families with older children.

translations.source: Mgbe ị na-agafe Ebe ugwu Baltic n’oge oyi, lelee ebe kabịn ahụ, dị ka ịgafe okwute mmiri na-akpata mkpọtụ dị nnọọ egwu maka ndị ọ kacha metụta.
translations.reference: If crossing the Northern Baltic in winter, check the cabin location, as going through ice causes quite horrible noise for those most affected.
translations.hypothesis: When traveling through the Baltic States in winter, watch out for black ice, as driving conditions can be tricky for even experienced drivers.

translations.source: Njem nnyagharị nke Senti Piitasbọg gụnyere oge n'ime obodo. Ndị njem nke njem nnyagharị bụ ndị ewezụgara site n'ụmụ ihe ndị achọrọ maka visa (lelee usoro ahụ).
translations.reference: Saint Petersburg cruises include time in town. Cruise passengers are exempted from visa requirements (check the terms).
translations.hypothesis: The St. Petersburg Rally included a stop in the city. The participants of the rally were detained after the bus they were travelling in was stopped for a visa check (see process).

translations.source: Ụlọ chaa chaa gasị na-eme ihe niile ịhụ na ndị mmadụ mefuru oge na ego ha niile. Windo na elekere anaghị adịkewe n'ime ha; ọzọ, ụzọ ọpụpụ na-arakarị ahụ ịchọta.
translations.reference: Casinos typically make many efforts to maximize time and money spent by guests. Windows and clocks are usually absent, and exits can be hard to find.
translations.hypothesis: Tourist-trap restaurants invariably charge exorbitant prices. Windows and doors are often missing or boarded up, and the exits are sometimes hard to find.

translations.source: Ha na-enwekarị nri pụrụ iche, mmanya na ụmụ onyinye ntụrụndụ, iji debe ndị ọbịa n'ọnọdụ dị mma, ma debe ha n'ogige ahụ.
translations.reference: They usually have special food, drink and entertainment offers, to keep guests in a good mood, and keep them at the premise.
translations.hypothesis: They usually offer a full range of services, including food, drinks, and entertainment, to keep guests happy and on the premises.

translations.source: Ụfọdụ ebe mgbakọ na-enye ụmụ ihe ọn̄ụn̄ụ na-eme n'anya n'efu. Mana, mmanya ogbugbu na-egbochi echiche, ma ndị nille na-agba chaa chaa nke ọma mara mkpa nke ọ dị ịnọ n'ezi echiche.
translations.reference: Some venues offer alcoholic beverages on the house. However, drunkenness impairs judgement, and all good gamblers know the importance of staying sober.
translations.hypothesis: Some bars and clubs offer free peanuts or other snacks. However, alcohol impairs judgment, and heavy drinkers often seriously underestimate the risks.

translations.source: Onye ọ bụla nke na-aga ịnya ụgbọ ala ya elu latitude maọbụ n’elu ugwu gafere, kwesịrị ịtụle ihe enwere ike ịbụ oge snow, ice, ma ọ bụ oke oyi.
translations.reference: Anyone who's going to drive at high latitudes or over mountain passes should consider the possibility of snow, ice, or freezing temperatures.
translations.hypothesis: Anyone going to a high-elevation or high-latitude region should be aware of the possibility of snow, ice, and extreme cold.

translations.source: N’okporo ụzọ ebe ais na sno dị, nrapara dị ala nakwa ịnweghị ike ịnya moto n'elu ya dịka ị nọ na asfalt nkịtị.
translations.reference: On icy and snowy roadways, friction is low and you cannot drive as if you were on bare asphalt.
translations.hypothesis: On the other hand, the ice roads are low traffic and you can ride your bike on them just like on normal asphalt roads.

translations.source: N'oge ụmụ oke ozuzo okwute mmiri, sinoo ga-ezu iji mee ka ị tọọ nwere ike izo n'ime ntakịrị oge.
translations.reference: During blizzards, enough snow to get you stuck can fall in very little time.
translations.hypothesis: During periods of heavy rain, the falls may be obscured by the spray.

translations.source: Enwere ike igbochi mgbàràìhè site na ịda ma ọ bụ ịfụ sinoo ma ọ bụ site na umu irighiri mmiri ma ọ bụ mmiri kpụkọrọ akpụkọ na windo ụgbọala.
translations.reference: Visibility may also be restricted by falling or blowing snow or by condensation or ice on vehicle windows.
translations.hypothesis: Sunlight can be reduced by closing or shading windows or using tinted car windows.

translations.source: N'aka nke ọzọ, ụmụ ọnọdụ okwute mmiri na sinoo bụ ihe nkịtị n'ọtụtụ mba, ma ụmụ ụgbọala na-anyagharị n'enweghị nsogbu afọ niile.
translations.reference: On the other hand, icy and snowy conditions are normal in many countries, and traffic goes on mostly uninterrupted all year round.
translations.hypothesis: On the other hand, conditions on the sea are normal in most countries, and the shipping season is open all the year round.

translations.source: Safari nwere ike ịbụ ihe kachasị akpọta ndị njem nlereanya na Afrịka ma bụrụkwa ihe kachasị atụ ha n'anya.
translations.reference: Safaris are perhaps the greatest tourism draw in Africa and the highlight for many visitors.
translations.hypothesis: Safari can be the most rewarding and the most disappointing experience for a tourist in Africa.

translations.source: Okwu bụ safari n’ojiji ama ama pụtara ime njem n’ofe ala ileleanụ ọhịa Afrịka dị ịtụnanya, tụnadị na savanna.
translations.reference: The term safari in popular use refers to overland travel to view the stunning African wildlife, particularly on savanna.
translations.hypothesis: The word safari comes from an Arabic word for journey, and originally referred to a journey through the African interior, typically the savanna.

translations.source: Ụmụanụmanụ ụfọdụ, dịka enyi ga na mgbara ga, na-abịaru nso n’ụgbọala ma ngwaọrụ izugbe dị mma ga-enye gị ohere iji hụ ha nke ọma.
translations.reference: Some animals, such as elephants and giraffes, tend to approach closely to cars and standard equipment will allow good viewing.
translations.hypothesis: Some animals, such as the prairie dog, are shy and will only come out when the area is clear of humans.

translations.source: Ọdụm, agụogbu na agụ na-eme ihere mgbe ụfọdụ ma ị ga-ahụ na nke ọma karịa n'iji baịnokụlaasị.
translations.reference: Lions, cheetahs and leopards are sometimes shy and you will see them better with binoculars.
translations.hypothesis: The bottom, the blade and the edge are sometimes serrated and you will find it more efficient to use a bayonet.

translations.source: Safari ngagharị (nke a na-akpọkwa "njem ọhịa", "safari ọrịrị", maọbụ "nzọụkwụ") gbakwunyere ịrị ugwu ruo awa ole na ole maọbụ ọtụtụ ụbọchị.
translations.reference: A walking safari (also called a "bush walk", "hiking safari", or going "footing") consists of hiking, either for a few hours or several days.
translations.hypothesis: A safari (also called a walking safari, bush safari, or overland safari) is usually combined with a few days or weeks of camping in the bush.

translations.source: Engwuregwu Paralimpiks ga-eme site n'Ọgọọst 24 ruo na Septemba 5 2021. A ga-eme ụfọdụ emume n'ebe ndị ọzọ gburugburu Japan.
translations.reference: The Paralympics will take place from 24 August to 5 September 2021. Some events will be held in other locations throughout Japan.
translations.hypothesis: The Paralympic Games will be held from 24 August to 5 September 2021. Some events will be held at venues outside of Tokyo.

translations.source: Tokyo ga-abụ naanị obodo Eshia nke kwadoro asọmpi nke oge okpomọkụ ugboro abụọ, ebe akwadoro egwuregwu ahụ na 1964.
translations.reference: Tokyo will be the only Asian city to have hosted two summer Olympics, having hosted the games in 1964.
translations.hypothesis: Tokyo will be the only Asian city to have hosted the summer olympics twice, after being awarded the games in 1964.

translations.source: Ọ bụrụ na ị kwụrụ ụgwọ maka ụgbọelu gị na ebe obibi gị maka 2020 tupu ekwuputa myigharịrị oge, i nwere ike inwe ọnọdụ tara akpụ.
translations.reference: If you booked your flights and accommodation for 2020 before the postponement was announced, you may have a tricky situation.
translations.hypothesis: If you had already paid for your 2020 pilgrimage before the announcement of the ban, you may be in a tricky situation.

translations.source: Iwu nkagbu na-adị iche iche, mana ka ọ dị na Maachị gara aga ọtụtụ n'ime ụmụ iwu nkagbu dabere na njecorona agbatịghị ruo Julaị 2020, mgbe ahazirioge Olumpiks ahụ.
translations.reference: Cancellation policies vary, but as of late March most coronavirus-based cancellation policies don't extend to July 2020, when the Olympics had been scheduled.
translations.hypothesis: The specific rules varied, but as of March 2020 most of the COVID-related border restrictions were lifted by July 2020 in time for the Olympics.

translations.source: Ọ bụ ihe atụwara anya ya na ọtụtụ tiketị emume ga-adị ọnụ n'etiti ¥2,500 na ¥130,000, ya na tiketị a na-ahụkarị na-adị ọnụ ruo ihe dị ka ¥7,000.
translations.reference: It's expected that most event tickets will cost between ¥2,500 and ¥130,000, with typical tickets costing around ¥7,000.
translations.hypothesis: Expectedly, most event tickets would range between 2,500 and 130,000 yen, with the average ticket costing around 7,000 yen.

translations.source: Ide akwa butụ mmiri nwere ike inyere ha aka ịkọ. Ọtụtụ ụlọ nkwarị akụ nwere otu igwe ndetị akwa na bọọdụ ide akwa dị adị maka mgbaziri, ọbụlagodi ma otu anọghị anọ n'ime ụlọ ahụ.
translations.reference: Ironing damp clothes can help them dry. Many hotels have an iron and ironing board available for loan, even if one is not present in the room.
translations.hypothesis: Learning to knit can help them to relax. Many libraries have a knitting circle or club, or even just a knitting corner.

translations.source: Ọ bụrụ na igwe ndetị akwa adịghị adị, ma ọ bụ ọ bụrụ na ọ masịghị gị iyi sọks edere ede, mgbe ahụ ị nwere ike ịnwa iji otu igwe ịkọ ntutu, ma ọ dịrị.
translations.reference: If an iron isn't available, or if you don't fancy wearing ironed socks, then you can try using a hairdryer, if available.
translations.hypothesis: If you don't have a cable knit sweater, or if you're not into wearing printed socks, then you can try a simple one-color cable knit.

translations.source: Kpachara anya ka akwa ghara ịdị oke ọkụ (nke a nwere ike ime ka akwa hịkpọọ, maọbụ ọ ka njọ, o nwere ike ịgba ọkụ).
translations.reference: Be careful not to allow fabric to become too hot (which can cause shrinkage, or in extreme cases, scorch).
translations.hypothesis: Be careful that the cloth does not get too hot (this can cause burns, or at worst, set the cloth on fire).

translations.source: E nwere ọtụtụ ụzọ e ji eme ka mmiri dị ọcha, ụfọdụ kara dị ire maka ụmụ ihe iyi egwu pụrụ iche.
translations.reference: There are different ways of purifying water, some more effective against specific threats.
translations.hypothesis: There are many ways to make water safe, some are more appropriate for specific risk factors.

translations.source: N'ebe ụfọdụ isi mmiri n'ọkụ ruo otu nkeji ezuola, n'ebe ndị ọzọ achọrọ ọtụtụ nkeji.
translations.reference: In some areas boiling water for a minute is enough, in others several minutes are needed.
translations.hypothesis: In some cases a minute or so is enough, in other cases several minutes are needed.

translations.source: Ụmụ m̀yọ̀ na-adị iche n’ịdị irè, ma ọ bụrụ na ị nwee nchebara echiche, mgbe ahụ ị kwesịrị itule uche ịzụ mmiri gị n’ime otu karama amachiri siye na otu ụlọ ọrụ nwere aha ọma.
translations.reference: Filters vary in effectiveness, and should you have a concern, then you should consider buying your water in a sealed bottle from a reputable company.
translations.hypothesis: The quality of the water varies, and if you are concerned, you should consider drinking only bottled water from a reputable brand.

translations.source: Ndị njem nwere ike ịhụta ụmụ anụ ọtapịa ndị nke ha na-amaghị n'ebe ụlọ ha.
translations.reference: Travellers may encounter animal pests that they are not familiar with in their home regions.
translations.hypothesis: Visitors may see animals in the wild that they did not know lived in the area.

translations.source: Pesti nwere ike imebi nri, kpata Pests can spoil food, cause mmeka ahụ, ma ọ bụ n’ọnọdụ ka njọ kpata mmeghachi omume nfụkasị, kesaa venọm, ma ọ bụ ọrịa ofufe.
translations.reference: Pests can spoil food, cause irritation, or in a worse case cause allergic reactions, spread venom, or transmit infections.
translations.hypothesis: Pests can damage food crops, cause harm to humans, or, in worst cases, lead to allergic reactions, share venom, or transmit infectious diseases.

translations.source: Ụmụ ọrịa na-efe efe n’onwe ha, ma ọ bụ ụmụ anụmanụ dị egwu nwere ike imerụ ma ọ bụ gbuo mmadụ n’ike, a na-ghị etozukarị oke dị ka ụmụ ahụhụ a na-achọghị.
translations.reference: Infectious diseases themselves, or dangerous animals that can injure or kill people by force, do not usually qualify as pests.
translations.hypothesis: Patients may be bitten by mosquitoes, or by other animals such as dogs, which may also rarely transmit the infection.

translations.source: Azụmaahịa na-enweghị ụtụ isi bụ ohere ịzụ ngwaahịa ndị ewezụgara site na ụtụ isi n’ụgwọ ndị ọzọ n’ebe ụfọdụ.
translations.reference: Duty free shopping is the opportunity to buy goods exempted from taxes and excises at certain locations.
translations.hypothesis: Duty-free shops are located in many international airports and other border crossings.

translations.source: Ndị njem na-aga mba ndị nwere nnukwu ụtụ isi nwere ike mgbe ụfọdụ ichekwa ọkpụrụkpụrụ ego, tụmadị na ngwaahịa dị ka ụmụ ihe ọn̄ụn̄ụ ndị na-aba n'anya na ụtaba.
translations.reference: Travellers bound for countries with heavy taxation can sometimes save a considerable amount of money, especially on products such as alcoholic beverages and tobacco.
translations.hypothesis: Travellers to high-cost countries may sometimes save money, especially on items such as alcoholic beverages and tobacco.

translations.source: Mgbatị ụzọ nọ n'etiti Point Marion na Fairmont na-enye ọnọdụ ịnya ụgbọala kachasị taa akpụ n'Okporoụzọ Buffalo-Pittsburg, na-agafe ọtụtụ oge site n'ọdịdịala azụ ọhịa dịpụrụ adịpụ.
translations.reference: The stretch between Point Marion and Fairmont presents the most challenging driving conditions on the Buffalo-Pittsburgh Highway, passing frequently through isolated backwoods terrain.
translations.hypothesis: The stretch of I-68 between Point Marion and Fairmont offers the most dramatic driving along the Buffalo-Pittsburg Trail, passing through a series of tunnels bored through the mountains.

translations.source: Oburu na imaatachabeghi ka esi anya ugboala n’okporouzo ime obodo, ume ahapukwala gi: uzo n’akpode akpode, uzo di wara wara na nkuku nko juru eju.
translations.reference: If you're not used to driving on country roads, keep your wits about you: steep grades, narrow lanes, and sharp curves predominate.
translations.hypothesis: If you're not used to hiking on rocky, steep terrain, take care: the path is often rough and the drop-offs are serious.

translations.source: Ókè ekwomọsọ ebipụtara dị obere karịa n'ụzọ ahụrụ anya na ngalaba ndị ọzọ gara aga ma ndị na-abịa abịa - na-abụkarị mph 35-40 (km/h 56-64) - ma nrubeisi siri ike na ha kara dị mkpa karịa otu ọzọ.
translations.reference: Posted speed limits are noticeably lower than in previous and subsequent sections — commonly 35-40 mph (56-64 km/h) — and strict obedience to them is even more important than otherwise.
translations.hypothesis: The top speed is lower than in other classes of cars and is usually 35–40 mph (56–64 km/h), and the emphasis is on safety over speed.

translations.source: Na mmata ihe, n'agbanyeghị, ọrụ ekwentị mkpààgagharị ka dị ike ebe a karịa ọtụtụ ogologo ụzọ ndị ọzọ ahụ, dịka ọmụmaatụ Ọhịa Pennsylvania ahụ.
translations.reference: Curiously, though, mobile phone service is much stronger here than along many other stretches of the route, e.g. the Pennsylvania Wilds.
translations.hypothesis: For the informed, however, the mobile phone industry is more competitive than most other industries, including the Pennsylvania coal industry.

translations.source: Pastrị ndị Jamini dị nnọọ mma; na Bavaria, ọ na-enwe ọtụtụ ihe ma dịkwa iche iche ka nke ndị Ọstrịa, agbata obi ha n'akụkụ ndịda.
translations.reference: German pastries are quite good, and in Bavaria, are quite rich and varied, similar to those of their southern neighbor, Austria.
translations.hypothesis: Jaminis are very good pastries; in Bavaria, they are made in many different forms, and are a speciality of the southern region.

translations.source: A na-ahụkarị ụmụ achịcha mkpụrụ osisi, e ji apụl eme achịcha mgbe niile n'afọ, ejikwa cheri na plọm eme achịcha n'oge sọma.
translations.reference: Fruit pastries are common, with apples cooked into pastries year round, and cherries and plums making their appearances during the summer.
translations.hypothesis: The most common are fruit bats, which normally eat fruit and flowers, and occasionally raid orchards and vineyards.

translations.source: Ọtụtụ ngwaahịa achịcha eghere eghe na Jamanị na-egosipụtakwa njirimara ụmụ alịmọndụ, hezelnọt, na mkpụrụ osisi ndị ọzọ. Achịcha ndị ama ama na-agakarị nke ọma ya na otu iko nke kọfị siri ike.
translations.reference: Many German baked goods also feature almonds, hazelnuts, and other tree nuts. Popular cakes often pair particularly well with a cup of strong coffee.
translations.hypothesis: Many German bakeries also produce a range of other pastries, cakes, and breads. The most popular fillings are usually combined with a strong black coffee.

translations.source: Ọ bụrụ na ị chọrọ ụmụ achịcha ndị pere mpe ma baakwa ụba, nwaa ihe na-ndabere na mpaghara a na-akpọ Berliner, Pfannkuchen ma ọ bụ Krapfen.
translations.reference: If you want some small though rich pastries, try what depending on region are called Berliner, Pfannkuchen or Krapfen.
translations.hypothesis: If you are in the mood for something small and sweet, try the Berliner, Pfannkuchen or Krapfen.

translations.source: Curry bu nri eji ngwa nri nke di iche iche esi, ana etinyekwa ya anu ma o bu akwukwo nri.
translations.reference: A curry is a dish based on herbs and spices, together with either meat or vegetables.
translations.hypothesis: Curry is a dish consisting of a sauce or gravy, often spiced, and usually served with rice.

translations.source: Kọrị nwere ike ịdị "akọrọ" maọbụ dị "mmiri mmiri", ọ dabeere na mmiri dị adị.
translations.reference: A curry can be either "dry" or "wet" depending on the amount of liquid.
translations.hypothesis: The snow can be "dry" or "wet", depending on the temperature.

translations.source: Ụmụ mpaghara imeala nke Ebe Ugwu Indịa na Pakistan, a na-ejikarị yogọọt n'ime ụmụ kọrị; n'ime Ebe Ndịda Indịa na mpaghara ndị ọzọ dị n'akụkụ mmiri nke okpuru kọntinent ahụ, a na-ejikarị mmiri ara akị oyibo.
translations.reference: In inland regions of Northern India and Pakistan, yogurt is commonly used in curries; in Southern India and some other coastal regions of the subcontinent, coconut milk is commonly used.
translations.hypothesis: In the Indian subcontinent and Pakistan, yoghurt is often used in the marinade; in the Indian Ocean and other coastal areas of the continent, coconut milk is often used instead.

translations.source: Ebe enwere agwaetiti 17,000 isi wee họrọ, nri Indonesia bụ aha gburugburu nke a na-akpọ ọtụtụ erimeri nke ọtụtụ mpaghara dị na mba ahụ niile.
translations.reference: With 17,000 islands to choose from, Indonesian food is an umbrella term covering a vast variety of regional cuisines found across the nation.
translations.hypothesis: With 17,000 islands to choose from, Indonesian cuisine is an umbrella term for the cuisines of many regions in the archipelago.

translations.source: Mana, e kwuo ya n'etinyeghi nkọwa ọbụla, ihe a na-achọkarị ikwu bụ nri ahụ si n'etiti na ọwụwa anyanwu nke nnukwu agwaetiti Java.
translations.reference: But, if used without further qualifiers, the term tends to mean the food originally from the central and eastern parts of the main island Java.
translations.hypothesis: However, without any further elaboration, this most probably refers to the traditional breakfast and lunch of the island of Java.

translations.source: Ugbu a ọ dị adị nke ukwuu na gburugburu òtù ụmụ agwaetiti ndị ahụ, nri Ndị Java nwere njirimara nri ndị etijuru ngwa nri na mfe n’usoro, ekpomeekpo ahụ kara dị ike Ndị Java kara nwee mmasị na ya ndị nke bụ ahụekere achịcha kpuchiri, ose, shuga (tụmadị shuga akị Ndị Java) na ngwa nrị ndị ọzọ nwere usi ọma.
translations.reference: Now widely available throughout the archipelago, Javanese cuisine features an array of simply seasoned dishes, the predominant flavorings the Javanese favor being peanuts, chillies, sugar (especially Javanese coconut sugar) and various aromatic spices.
translations.hypothesis: Nowadays, especially around tourist areas, many Javanese restaurants have adopted Western-style service, and the cuisine has been influenced by the use of many Western ingredients and techniques. Javanese cuisine is known for its rich and complex flavors, often incorporating a wide range of spices, herbs, and other flavorings such as peanuts, palm sugar (gula jawa), and tempeh.

translations.source: Ihe nkonye ụkwụ bụ ihe na-ejide ụkwụ onye na-agba ịnyịnya nke na-awụdata n'akụkụ abụọ site oche elu ịnyịnya.
translations.reference: Stirrups are supports for the rider's feet that hang down on either side of the saddle.
translations.hypothesis: The blade is the part of the skates that rests on the ice and is hinged to the bottom of the boot.

translations.source: Ha na-ewetara onye na-agba ha nnukwu nnọsi ike mana ha nwere ike inwe nsogbu nchekwa maka na ụkwụ onye na-agba ya pụrụ ịkpachi n'ime ha.
translations.reference: They provide greater stability for the rider but can have safety concerns due to the potential for a rider's feet to get stuck in them.
translations.hypothesis: They are very responsive to the rider, but can be hard to control for inexperienced riders.

translations.source: Ọ bụrụ na esị n'elu ịnyịnya tụpụ onye na-anya ya mana ụkwụ onye ahụ ekonye n'ekike ịnyịnya, ịnyịnya nwere ike ịsekpụrụ ya na-aga ma ọ gbaa ọsọ. Iji belata ihe egwu a, enwere ụfọdụ ihe mkpachapụ anya enwere ike ime.
translations.reference: If a rider is thrown from a horse but has a foot caught in the stirrup, they could be dragged if the horse runs away. To minimize this risk, a number of safety precautions can be taken.
translations.hypothesis: If the skater falls to the side, the skates will cause him or her to fall in that direction, and the skater may be dragged along as the skates move. To reduce this risk, there are some precautions that can be taken.

translations.source: Na mbụ, ọtụtụ n’ime ndị na-anya na-eyi akpụkpọ ụkwụ ọnyịnya ndị nwere kọị kọị na okpuru dị nrọ ma pee mpe.
translations.reference: First, most riders wear riding boots with a heel and a smooth, quite narrow, sole.
translations.hypothesis: Originally, most of the dancers wore heavy, clunky shoes with bells on the bottom.

translations.source: Ọzọ, ụfọdụ sadụl, ọkachasị sadụl Bekee, nwere ebe nchekwa na-ekwe ka akpụkpọ anụ si na sadụl dapụ ma onye na-anya anya sere ya laa azụ mgbe ọ na-ada.
translations.reference: Next, some saddles, particularly English saddles, have safety bars that allow a stirrup leather to fall off the saddle if pulled backwards by a falling rider.
translations.hypothesis: Additionally, some sleds, especially toboggans, have a runner that is slightly curved so that the sled naturally turns when tilted.

translations.source: Ndagwurugwuru Cochamó - ebe arimelu nwere ogo kachasị elu nke Chile, a mara dị ka Yosemite nke Ndịda Amerịka, ya na ụdị dị iche iche nke ụmụ nnukwu ahụaja kọnkịrị na nnukwu nkume.
translations.reference: Cochamó Valley - Chile's premier climbing destination, known as the Yosemite of South America, with a variety of granite big walls and crags.
translations.hypothesis: The Carretera Austral - Southern Highway, is a scenic route that parallels the Andes Mountains and passes through a variety of landscapes including fjords, glaciers, lakes, and rainforests.

translations.source: Ụmụ ọnụ ugwu kachasị elu gụnyere nlenle ndị magburu onwe ha site n'elu ebe ndị ahụ. Ndị na-arị elu si n'akụkụ ụwa niile na-awapụta mgbe niile ụzọ ọhụrụ site n'ahụaja ya niile e nwere ike isi wapụta ụzọ nke anaghị agwụ agwụ.
translations.reference: Summits include breath-taking views from peaks. Climbers from all parts of the world are continually establishing new routes amongst its endless potential of walls.
translations.hypothesis: The highest peaks include some of the most challenging climbs in the world. Climbers from around the world regularly attempt new routes up its many faces, some of which have yet to be successfully ascended.

translations.source: Kpoda-ugwu egwuregwu-snow, bu nke gunyere igba igwe mmiri ski na snowboard, bu egwuregwu amaara-amaara nke gbasara ikpoda ala site n’elu n’ogige juputara na snow jiri igwe ski na snowboard eyigidere n’ukwu gi.
translations.reference: Downhill snowsports, which include skiing and snowboarding, are popular sports involving sliding down snow-covered terrain with skis or a snowboard attached to your feet.
translations.hypothesis: Alpine skiing, also known as downhill skiing, is a popular sport that involves descending a snow-covered slope on skis.

translations.source: Egwuregwu skii bụ otu isi ihe omume n'etiti ndị ọ na-amasị, mgbe ụfọdụ a na-amara ya dị ka "ski bums," na-eme atụmatụ nke oge ezumike niile gburugburu ime skii n'otu ebe kpọmkwem.
translations.reference: Skiing is a major travelling activity with many enthusiasts, occasionally known as "ski bums," planning entire vacations around skiing at a particular location.
translations.hypothesis: Skiing is a favourite pastime for many, sometimes known as "ski bums", planning their whole year around a ski trip to a particular location.

translations.source: Egwuregwu ski eteela ọ nọ — ụmụ eserese esere n'ọgba kemgbe 5000 BC na-egosi ndị egwuregwu ski!
translations.reference: The idea of skiing is very old — cave paintings depicting skiers date back as far as 5000 BC!
translations.hypothesis: The sport of skiing has ancient roots -- cave paintings from 5000 B.C. show what appear to be skiers!

translations.source: Igwu skii na mgbada ugwu dị ka otu egwuregwu gara azụ ruo opekata mpe ọ bụrụ na arị afọ iri na asaa, ma n’ime 1861 òtù egwuregwu skii ntụrụndụ nke mbụ bụ nke emepere site n’aka Ndị Nọọwei n’ime Ọstrelịa.
translations.reference: Downhill skiing as a sport goes back to at least the 17th century, and in 1861 the first recreational ski club was opened by Norwegians in Australia.
translations.hypothesis: Skiing and snowboarding as a sport have been around for at least 7,000 years, and the first ski jumping competition was held in Norway in 1861.

translations.source: Njem mfe ski: A na-akpọkwa omume a bakkọntrị ski, ije nlegharị anya ski maọbụ ịrị ugwu ski.
translations.reference: Backpacking by ski: This activity is also called backcountry ski, ski touring or ski hiking.
translations.hypothesis: Cross-country skiing: Also known as Nordic skiing, or ski touring.

translations.source: O metụtara mana ọ naghị agụnyekarị ọdịdị njem nleta ski keugwu ma ọ bụ egwuregwu ịrị elu ugwu, nke ikpeazụ ndị a e mere n'ọdịdịala kpodara ekpoda ma na-achọ ụmụ ski na buutu kara sie ike.
translations.reference: It is related to but usually not involving alpine style ski touring or mountaineering, the latter ones done in steep terrain and requiring much stiffer skis and boots.
translations.hypothesis: It is related to but distinct from the sports of alpine skiing and snowboarding, the latter two sports having evolved from earlier forms of skiing and requiring specialized equipment and footwear.

translations.source: Chee echiche maka ụzọ esi egwu egwuregwu skii dị ka ụzọ e si aga njem ije nke yiri.
translations.reference: Think of the skiing route as of a similar hiking route.
translations.hypothesis: Think of the ways to go skiing as the ways to go hiking.

translations.source: N'ọnọdụ dị mma i nwere ike ịgarute ntoanya buru ibu karịa ịga ije - mana ọ na-ara ahụ tupu i rute ekwomọsọ nke ime skii ofe mba n'enweghị otu akpa azụ dị arụ n'ime mkpọwaraụzọ akwadogwere.
translations.reference: In good conditions you will be able to cover somewhat greater distances than walking – but only very seldom you will get the speeds of cross country skiing without a heavy backpack in groomed tracks.
translations.hypothesis: In good conditions you can reach the bottom of the canyon with a normal walking stick - but it is a painful experience to get to the bottom of the canyon without any ropes or any other equipment.
